text: A friend and I had dinner here on Sunday, November 13, and couldn't have been happier. We didn't have a reservation, but when we called, we were welcomed and told they'd accommodate us when we arrived. That's exactly what happened when we did arrive. We were interested in sharing some dishes to maximize flavor experiences and minimize calories, so we decided on the calamari and rock shrimp with tempura veggies as an appetizer, and then a special entree of the night plus roasted veggies. We came to this decision with the help of our excellent server who clearly wanted us to have a great evening. Wines by the glass are very diverse, and quite reasonable. We each enjoyed a glass to our taste that paired well with the food we had ordered. Now to discuss the food: Calamari-Rock shrimp-tempura vegetables: delicious and perfectly prepared with an amazing variety of veggies (including fennel!); perhaps a bit more seafood would have been nice, but we were happy. Entree: this special was a trio of seafoods: grilled salmon with a polenta cake, sea bass with mushroom risotto, and fried trout with a bit of salad. We split each of these, and still had plenty of food, and each of the trio tasted excellent (tiny quibbles: the salmon could have been cooked a bit less, and everything needed some salt and pepper). Grilled vegetables: asparagus, portabellas, carrots, squash, fennel, green beans and more were on this platter. They were the perfect accompaniment to our fish. A couple of the carrot slices were cut too thickly, and were therefore uncooked, and their balsamic-brie dipping sauce did not contribute anything, but this is minor. We left the restaurant both sated and happy. We WILL return.

text: I've been getting my hair done at the Hair Suite for over ten years now. My mother was a client of a stylist that used to work there, and took me as a young teenager when I decided I wanted to dye my hair. In the years I've been a client my hair has gone from near platinum blonde to black and back to blonde, from elbow length to chin length and I have never ever left unhappy. Linda (a stylist and also the owner) is one of the nicest people you will ever meet and does a seriously fantastic job on my hair. She is straightforward and will let you know what is possible to accomplish in one session and will work with you to get the look you want. A few years back I got a little too friendly with my flat iron and broke off a giant chunk of hair right near my face. Linda gave me a cut that helped to blend it as it grew out and no one could even tell it was there! She is also great with color -- I get tons of compliments on my hair and owe it all to her. Back when myspace was the thing, someone found a picture of me and coincidentally brought it into the Hair Suite asking for my cut/color. As far as price -- I can't commit to a hairstyle or color for more than six months, so the price changes per visit but I don't think I have ever paid more than 160 including tip (cut, single process color, highlight, style). I moved to Philadelphia in 2007 and am in close proximity to several "high end" salons and still drive back to Cherry Hill to get my hair done. As long as they are open, I will continue to get my hair done at Hair Suite. Don't let the location or the fact that a big portion of the clientele are older women deter you -- I'll be honest, I am in my early-mid twenties and am almost always the youngest person in the salon. The atmosphere is a little lacking and the salon looks a little dated, but to be honest if these women operated out of a warehouse I wouldn't even care. They are that good!

Rather than turn away a customer, he could have checked to see if there were anyone else within Donnelly's with the necessary experience. Considering there are over 17,000 Levittown homes, Donnelly's really should send out someone experienced with the way these houses are set up, if they want to continue saying that they do work in Levittown. We contacted another plumber who has worked in Levittown for years and he knew exactly what to do and only had to replace 4 tiles. Guess I know who I'm calling for any future plumbing needs. No kinks even though they have only been open for a few weeks. Both appetizers were good-- homemade chips with garlic aioli and Devil's on Horseback. The main courses my table shared were also above expectation. The fish and chips were both good, the beef and puddings were well presented, at the right temperature,and tasty and the chicken pie was substantial. The service was friendly and attentive. Everyone on staff we met was a cheerful booster. Good to see. The crowd while we were there was low on both pretence and irony. That, I would wager is par for the course at an English pub and the delivery of a happy crowd, both patrons and staff is more important than whatever defects the decor had. I think the decor was fine, if a little minimalist and bright. I sure wouldn't want to decorate a restaurant, let alone an English Pub in Nashville. Eveyone has their idea of how it should look. I can tell you how a hot chicken shack SHOULD look like; I live in this town and know it well enough. But being 4,000 miles from authenticity makes having the RIGHT idea vary wildly. Add to that Yelp, where everyone is an expert (lord knows I am) and you really can't win for losing. Glad they didn't invest too much in that fool's errand. text: It's no wonder that Franklin Mortgage & Investment Co is so highly acclaimed. Then you descend the steps into an unassuming black door (no windows) and you enter a different era. The servers are wearing plaid shirts, jeans, and suspenders. The room is dimly lit with a few tables and a bar top. Now you see why the line is worth the wait. The crowd control at the door means a relaxed, non-crowded experience at the bar. And you never get rushed out. As for the drinks, they come pretty strong, with lots of citrus flavors, cucumbers, mint, and other delicious concoctions. If you don't want something on the menu, get it off the menu, or ask the bartender to make you something you might like. I had the Emma Frost and the Killer Bees on the Swarm. The problems first started when I checked-in, and was given my room key, etc. The room I went to was already occupied by someone else. Luckily, it was someone I knew (we were all traveling on business together), so there wasn't a huge issue there. They moved me to another room. Due to the "double booking" of the rooms, they offered me complimentary cheese and wine, and said it would be right up. Well, I waited and waited for as long as I could (I had dinner plans, so I couldn't wait all night!), and I tried calling the front desk, who transferred me to room service, and no one from room service ever picked up - so I gave up. Upon leaving for dinner, I mentioned this to the manager, who apologized and promised there would be complimentary cookies and beverages in my room when I returned. When I returned, there were not any cookies to be found. I went downstairs for a drink with my coworker, and we went to the front desk afterwards to inquire about the situation. They told me they weren't aware of the "arrangement" but they did inform me that they were out of cookies.... Well, when I finally went up to my room that night - surprise! There was cake! And the cheese and wine! I thought things were FINALLY looking up! But the next morning, my bill came under the door - they had me checking out that day, when I actually was staying there another day. I had to go to the front desk, and have the entire situation sorted out - which it was sorted out, but at this point, I felt like I had spent too much time bringing all of these problems to their attention! After I finally checked out the following day, I thought my problems with this hotel were over - until I saw that they overcharged my credit card by $106!!! What's worse, is that when I noticed the discrepancy, I called the hotel, was transferred, and left a message that was not returned. I then called again (which I should not have to do - I would hope it would be them following up!!!), at which point I finally talked to someone, who told me that my credit card was charged the amount that someone else's card was meant to be charged - they mixed up our credit cards! Quite honestly, this created a hassle for submitting my expense report at work - and between the other problems I've mentioned, the fire alarm going off endlessly one night (scared the crap out of me - I see this happened to several others who left reviews, which doesn't make me hopeful that they're trying to fix the problem), and the "dusty" feel to the rooms, I don't think I'll stay here again.

text: Saturday, 12/18/2010 - 8pm reservations for two Went here for dinner with my special girl. She'd been dying to come here for some time, but I admit I was a little apprehensive given my hit-or-miss luck with upscale / "fine dining" restaurants. Plus I scoped out the menu online before going and nothing really stood out for me (forgive me for being a simpleton, but I don't know what half the things on these types of menus mean haha). The things I do for love ;-). We'd eaten at restaurants on Penn's Landing before, so the view was nothing new to us, though I have to admit, there is a high "cool factor" with Moshulu. The ship itself has a lot of history, and was very elegantly decorated (despite some comments in other reviews). It definitely feels like a place for a special night upon entering. Dinner starts out with complimentary rolls w/ butter. We then ordered a side of mac n' cheese and the moo shu duck for appetizers. The mac n cheese had a truffled crust and was served at a very good temperature (warm). Though it looks small, the serving size was good to split between two as an appetizer. Both the mac n cheese and moo shu duck were very good. She had the Maine Diver Scallops, which was voted 2010 Philly Cook's Dish of the Year. I tried some and it was very good. My Wild Mushroom Crusted Mahi Mahi was a bit dry though. The serving size for my Mahi Mahi was large and unexpected given the type of restaurant ("upscale"). We closed dinner with the Moshulu Coupe. I'm going to describe it as a vanilla ice cream w/ bits of chocolate "cake" that was very good (the simpleton in me). Service was very good. Definitely felt our waiter was attentive but not overbearing. I definitely enjoyed Moshulu, and the ambiance was probably a large part of why (very romantic). It just feels like a special place for a special occasion. The food was overall very good, though very disappointed with my entrée (the Mahi Mahi was dry). The price is actually very reasonable with all things considered. Appetizers from $8 up, entrees from $14-$20, dessert $10. You do have to pay for parking ($10??), but I believe that is typical for the area. I'd love to come back when the weather is good enough to eat and/or hang out on the boat's deck. Highly recommended. Overall 4.5 stars (rounded up to 5). (SEE PHOTOS FOR FOOD)

text: This is a must try spot. This is the sort of restaurant that you might passby and not give a second thought to it. The small exterior is unremarkable and a sign simple reads El Tule Mexican Restaurant. Right away my mind conjurs images of tacos and burritos and Mariache music. El Tule has an expansive menu -- one Peruvian and one Mexican. My companion ordered a vegetarian lasagna from the Mexican menu. I ordered from the Peruvian menu. What a treat to be able to eat authentic recipes from Peru right here in Lambertville! The owners themselves, a brother and sister, are Peruvian. The food is freshly and wonderfully prepared. My order was photograph worthy, in fact, arriving on two plates each skillfully plated as an edible work of art. On one dish was Ceviche de Camarones: "Close your eyes and enjoy this treasure of a ceviche that will take you back to my cherished Peruvian cost. Our succulent shrimp ceviche is marinated in lime juice, garlic and aji amarillo served with red onions, sweet potatoes, Peruvian corn and Inca corn." On the other dish was a trio: Yuquitas Fritas with Huncaina Cream: "Crunchy fried yuca sticks served with a natural Andean cream made from milk, cheese and the secrets of Huncayo." Causa de Pollo: "Yellow potato cake inspired from a native land of the Inca. Enriched with yellow peppers and magical lemon, stuffed with chicken and vegetables and seasoned with Peruvian spices." Palta A La Reina: "Half of an avocado stuffed with shrimp, red onions, tomatoes and corn. Marinated with fresh cilantro-lime dressing." My meal was a little pricey at $27 but totally worth it. The wonderful flavors are still lingering in my mouth as I write. There is absolutely a selection of lesser priced items on the menus. My friend's Lasagna de Vegetales "Sautéed Eggplant, Zucchini, Roasted Red & Poblano Peppers, Mushrooms, & Queso, Layered Between Spinach Tortillas & Baked Until Golden Brown" was only $12. I had a taste and it was delish and very different from the better known Italian Lasagna. Wash your meal down with "Jaicama" (I believe the spelling is correct), a house drink that El Tule makes with hibiscus flowers. I will defiantely be back in the Spring to take advantage of the outdoor dining.

text: I've been to the jube several times for touring musical productions. My High School also had our grad ceremony here, and I was lucky enough to get to sing on stage, although that was before the renovations. The jubilee is a decent sized auditorium. I love the stadium seating, it's really hard to get a bad seat here - unless someone who's super tall sits in front of you. There are two balconies. The first balcony is really great, but I find the higher balcony harder to see from. The lobby is nicely decorated, with lots of local art. The drinks here are overpriced, so I tend to just go out somewhere after the show. The bathrooms are always clean, but get really busy. I don't like how the soap is integrated into the faucet system (unless that's been changed recently). It just means you're never 100% sure how clean your hands are, or your left with that soapy residue on them. As far as acoustics go for the audience they are great. The sound is quite good, and you won't have a problem hearing anything. I can say when I sang here I found the accoustics weren't great - this is for those performing, not the audience. But perhaps they were able to make some improvements with renovations. Still acoustically I don't think it compares to the Winspear Centre. Paid parking is available, but harder to come by with all the construction going on in the area. I would recommend taking the LRT where possible. The jubilee is a nice theatre in Edmonton, although it certainly doesn't have a classic feel to it, the way a theatre in New York would. Still unless your here for a rock concert I'd recommend getting dressed up. Nothing formal, just something nice. I always hate when I see people with ripped jeans and grubby t-shirts. Why not put on something clean if you're going for a night out?

A classic bait-and-switch: it isn't "2 for 1," it's "buy one drink and then your second drink is free." But when we told the bartender that we had a three hour drive ahead of us and we weren't planning on a second drink, he was cool and just charged us for one. The drinks were terrible. text: This place is absolutely great. I just moved to Philly and frankly have not been very impressed with many of the restaurants here. Well, this restaurant is only a few minutes from my house, so I thought I'd give it a try. We started with a bowl of tom yum soup (an absolute must any time I go eat Thai food), curry puffs, and shrimp golden (ie fried shrimp rolls). They were all fantastic. The curry puff was flaky and perfect. The tom yum soup hit all the right notes of spicy and sour. For our main, we had yellow curry fried rice and crispy duck with sweet and sour sauce. Both of them were great. Dessert was fried ice cream and it was good, although not the best I've ever had. It was still pretty high up there on my list. The service was terrific. We went late and the waiter showed no impatience or annoyance that we would keep him working a while longer. He was very sweet and inquired about our needs while being unobtrusive about filling our water and taking our plates. He seemed genuinely pleased that we were raving about the food. The prices were also reasonable. I've spent twice as much at other places for the same food without the same quality and service and would have happily spent that much to eat here. I was just about to give up on Philly having any good Asian restaurants. I'm glad to see I was wrong. I'm definitely be coming here regularly. Within the first 15 minutes of wearing them in the kitchen I was slipping and sliding all over the place until I finally came close enough to taking a huge spill and took them off. I cleaned them up and brought them back..I understand if you don't accept used shoes but these shoes we're defective, they did not serve the purpose they advertised. However, rather than even bother to listen why I needed to return them the man kept repeating "I don't take used shoes" over and over again. Even I couldn't return the shoes to him, if it was a pleasant experience I wouldn't have walked away feeling so hurt by it but the careless and inconsiderate manner in which I was dealt with left me feeling exasperated. Clearly to this man, probably the owner, it was not his problem. I'm sure Ellgee's is great and worth checking out for people in the medical field needing scrubs and coats, however I personally won't risk such an experience again and will go online to shop with a brand I can trust.

text: My husband and I love to try different restaurants in Nashville every weekend. We live in Clarksville, so (needless to say) most of the restaurants are chains. First, the restaurant is in a "unique" location to say it nicely. However, once you step inside it is absolutely wonderful. The atmosphere is a cross between romantic, industrial and contemporary. It's perfect for a relaxing date night. There was music in the background but it wasn't overwhelming. Although it was a smaller building and was fairly crowded, we felt we still were in a private/quiet area during dinner. Ok, the cocktails are fabulous! They have modern/contemporary cocktails (which I would recommend trying) along with the "classic" cocktails. We were both very pleased with our selections. After having 4 different ones, I could honestly say all were my favorite! It does take about 10-15 minutes to receive your drink after you order it, but its worth the wait. The food was exceptional as well. I got the grilled trout (which was light and fresh) and my husband got the catfish (which was by far my favorite catfish dish I've ever tried). I will be getting that next time we go, which will probably be in the next couple of weeks. We ordered the fried green tomatoes for the appitizer. They were cooked perfectly and were paired up with a unique asian slaw that complemented the saltiness of the tomatoes. For dessert we enjoyed the cheesecake. It was decent but I will probably try a different dessert next time. It is a bit pricey and the bill will add up, especially if you decide to try multiple drinks! But it's totally worth it!!!!

text: Hadn't been to Lou Bocarrdi's in quite sometime. I remember coming in when the storms of 2006 had downed power to most of the city in the summer and it was one of the few places that was open. Walking in the place sports a lot of what I would call "character" but others may see as needing "repair". The door has a bar on it but you actually need to use the handle at the bottom to enter. It is a little unnerving attempting to open the door into the bar but it is something I'll remember in future visits. Since I was last here I don't know what exactly changed but the downstairs bar area and dining area seemed brighter and more open. I think there had to have been some work done to the dining area to the right of when you enter because of the paintings and the tables stationed there. I was warned by the waitress that it is quite cooler in that area of the restaurant during the winter months. I guess I really noticed the downstairs dining area because of the window that looks out onto the Southwest/Magnolia split. The bar looks like it is from the 30's or 40's and is typical for what you would find at most other places in the area. There was one TV in the place located above the bar. Past the bar when you walk in is a set of stairs and two small rooms with tables which I would consider the main dining area. I don't think any of the tables are larger than a 4 top which is OK in my book because this restaurant, to me, is more for an intimate setting than for large groups. The walls in the second room have really beautiful mural paintings on them, compound that with the dim lighting it is almost like you are in an old museum. The menu has something for just about anyone on it and at all different price ranges as well. We started off with some garlic cheese bread. I went with the Tortellini which, all of the pasta dishes and entrees come with a salad and my mother went with the Gnocchi. The salad was a typical Hill restaurant salad served with lots of provel cheese and was very good. The Tortellini was very good. You have the option of choosing red or white sauce and I took the white. It was very rich and creamy with mushrooms in it. Mom's Gnocchi was good with the red sauce but she did comment that the shrimp were very tiny in size. I tried a bite and thought it was very tasty aside from the size of the Shrimp. All in all, the service was excellent and our waitress was very friendly and we even chatted a bit as the place was kind of slow. I definitely will come back because of all of the things on the menu I wanted to try. Based on past experiences I have to say their pizza is also pretty good for a Saint Louis style.

text: While driving home from San Luis Obispo to Orange County, I had a tire blow out on me. I put my donut spare on and drove 15 miles to the nearest town, Goleta. I called every tire place in the Santa Barbara area. Only Bob Woolevers both sold used tires AND had a tire ("a tire" is literal as I was told they had only one) my size. I couldn't afford a new tire; I had no credit card with me and only $50 cash on hand-and I would have to use the remaining balance from a used tire purchase for gas. I was told on the phone they had one tire my size in stock and that it would be $30 total, balanced/mounted/installed. When I got there, the guy brought out one of the baldest tires I've ever seen. I was appalled and immediately pointed out the total lack of tread on the outside, but was told it was a good tire, if it was bad they wouldn't sell it. I proceeded to buy the tire for one reason only - I was stranded and had absolutely no choice. When my tire blew, it was late at night and all businesses were closed, forcing me to spend the entire night sleeping in my car waiting for morning until shops opened. Driving home on the donut spare wasn't an option, as I've read that it's dangerous; you can't really exceed 50mph and you should never drive more than 50-70 miles on it-I was easily twice that distance from home. As tire professionals, Bob Woolevers knew that tire should never have been sold, much less placed on a traveling motorist's vehicle (I'd mentioned I was on my way home to OC). This, in my honest opinion, was very unethical behavior on the part of Bob Woolevers' shop. I strongly recommend looking elsewhere-ANYwhere-if you are in need of a used tire or tires.

text: I would give this place more stars but the service was less than acceptable. The ambiance was excellent. A smallish restaurant in an old home was very French. The welcome into the restaurant and to our table was nice. They have a nice menu that has small, medium and large portions. We opted to choose from the small and medium, and a bottle of wine. From the small menu, we ordered a green salad, the soup of the day (which was a puree or vegetables) and crab cake. From the medium menu, we ordered the hand rubbed ribs and the barbecued shrimp. That was the order. I did not ask, but was not offered the option, but I expected the salad would come first (split in plates), then the soup and crab cake was the next course, then the ribs and shrimp. The salad came, split in two plates and then the server put the soup in the middle of the table as if we were going to stretch our spoons to get the soup. By the time we finished the salad, and I went to try the soup, it was tepid. As I was working on the soup, the crab cake, ribs and shrimp came all at once. Needless to say, it damped the entire meal. I think restaurants need to understand the meaning of tapas or izakaya style dining because it makes not sense to serve all the dishes at once, especially if there are only TWO PEOPLE! The whole idea of this type of dining is to take one's time to enjoy each dish. I was SOOOOO disappointed because these small things can ruin such a great experience. I certainly hope someone teaches this restaurant as well as others to take heed to the history of izakaya style dining. Go to Japan and learn from them since that is how they have always dined. Value wise, it was on the high end but that was to be expected. I would not have minded the price if the experience were better. I was so looking forward to this restaurant because my mother used to watch Emeril's cooking show all the time. Maybe my expectations were too high? I really do not think so. I would definitely recommend that you visit the restaurant but make it clear how you want your dishes to come out unless you do not mind eating everything at one time, which I do not.

text: Great location. The hotel is located on a quiet part of Chartres near the northeast end of the French Quarter and is very quiet at night. Based on the location and price, I expected to see a tiny, creaky old room with a bathroom in need of renovation, but I was pleasantly surprised by the relatively comfortable size, cleanliness, ample counter space around the sink, and fairly new toilet and tub. Based on those, this would have received at least 4 stars but... Morning noise. Although it is quiet at night, this is probably one of the noisiest hotels I have experienced in the morning. Starting around 8 or 9 am every morning, you will hear dumpsters rattling across the driveway several times. It is so incredibly loud, you will be jerked awake with a WTF?!? You can forget about sleeping in peacefully after a night of indulgence. If your room is near the office, you will also have to hear the often loud farewells between the hotel staff and guests leaving early. No Do Not Disturb signs or door latches. text: Let me begin by saying I had high expectations of this place because some foodie friends recommended it. First, they don't take reservations, so be prepared to wait. And wait. And wait. We decided to go there later, thinking we'd avoid a long wait. Wrong! Got there at 8:00 on a Friday night, put our name in, and was told it would be a 45 to 60-minute wait. If you have to wait, make sure you go on a nice evening so you can stand outside...the "bar" is more like a walkway/pass through to the dining room. If you can't sit at a table or belly up to the bar, be prepared to be elbowed, stepped on and bumped into every 2 seconds. When we were finally seated 75 minutes later, our bubbly waitress, Ashley, was at our table in just a few minutes. As she tried to share the evening's specials, half of the table couldn't hear because the noise level is DEAFENING!!!! Appetizers: We started with appetizers...smokey shrimp with grits and cole slaw, and flatbread with herbed goat cheese. I found the shrimp/grits appetizer tasty, while the flatbread was, well, flat. Just goat cheese spread on some plain bread. The entrees: being a pescatarian, there weren't many choices for me...trout or the striped bass special. I opted for the trout. While it was quite tasty and cooked properly, it was heavy on the salt. And I am not a fan of salty dishes. Others ordered the pork chop, the ribeye and the bass special. Everyone's comments: it's okay. Just okay. The desserts: I am a dessert person. Anything with sugar. Period. But, after perusing the menu, nothing really appealed to me. Which says alot because...did I mention I'm a dessert person? Those that ordered dessert ate their dessert quietly. Draw your own conclusions. Lesson learned: go to a new restaurant with no expectations, just in case.

text: Best burger ever??? I was in St. Petersburg for New Year's and found Fuzzy's late one night. Being from California, it was weird getting used to people smoking in bars. But, the people were cool, beer was cold, and the bartenders were friendly. I noticed they had a Steakburger for $1.99 and it sounded too good to be true. I asked the bartender if I should order the double burger and she said no, the burger is a pretty good size, so I went with her recommendation. And, it was an amazing burger, served with all the fixings, perfectly seasoned, and truly tasted like a tender ground steak in that bun. It was definitely one of the best burgers of my life. My date had a few bites of it too and she agreed, it was pretty awesome. But, I went back 2 days later after constantly having that burger in my head and that afternoon, it was just ok. The only explanation I can offer is, the night cook is a genius on the grill. I'll definitely give it another try the next time I'm out that way but if anyone else wants to give the day steakburger vs. the night steakburger experiment a try, I'd love to hear your results. 4/14/2012 update ------------------------- I made a 3rd trip to Fuzzy's to see if it really was a great burger. I have no idea what happened the first time I ate there. They must have cooked a steak right before my burger because every trip since then, it's just been an average burger. No juicy steak taste. Just a burger. No need for a 4th trip. Downgrading to 2 stars.

text: I'm a regular at the River/Campbell location and have had nothing but excellent service, so when I checked in on my phone I was surprised to see the low overall rating of this Gadabout. Then I went inside and realized why they had a lackluster following. Backstory: I'd run out of the facewash I use that I can only find at Gatabout (without having to order online, pay for shipping) and I was between appointments with my esthetician so I figured I'd pick some up at this location since it's right by my office. I also wanted one of the neck pillows they carry- it helps with shoulder pain, as I work in front of a computer all day, and my massage therapist recommended it. So I walked in and the layout just threw me off- the reception area is facing perpendicular to the door, so the receptionists are constantly looking to the left to greet people coming in the door, and when they face forward, they're actually looking out onto the stylists' floor. Weird. The overall ambience of the place is cold and industrial- a lot of bare metal and concrete and it just gives off a cold and uninviting vibe. I explained I just needed to pick up some face wash and went over to the products area to select my skincare stuff and a neck pillow. Then I realized that the reception area was in the MIDDLE of the salon! What the hell? That's so awkward! Anyway, I proceeded back to the reception area and the receptionist had already forgotten who I was! Seriously? I just spoke to you 30 seconds ago. So she asked what service I had done today- um, none. I just needed facewash. She looked so upset and confused and asked me at least two more times if I had an appointment, a service done, whatever. My coming in for no salon service and only buying salon products just really seemed to throw her off her game. I get that it's an unusual transaction, I didn't appreciate feeling like an inconvenience. She didn't offer me a bag, either. That's annoying. I get places trying to go green and all that crap, but if someone's hands are full, they might appreciate some kind of device to carry their merchandise. Oh, and their parking lot sucks.

text: In what once was Sam Seltzers, my partner and I dined at Landers 9/27 arriving at 6:30PM. We were quickly seated in a 3/4 empty dining room. We were acknowledged immediately. We had purchased a coupon from TravelZoo.com for $37.00 that provided 1 shared appetizer, 2 entrees valued up to 29.00/ea and, and 2 glasses of wine. The lettuce in the salad was about 2 days past its prime. Fifteen minutes into our meal the waitress approaches and explains that the prime rib is sold out. Remember we arrived at 6:30 in a Tampa Steakhouse. That is way too early to run out of something. Not sure what to order now we asked for the menu. We decided on grilled rib eye steak. The rib eye steak was excellent. We both ordered French fries and they arrived luke warm at best...more on the cold side. Okay so why did I give this restaurant 2 stars. The hits were the steak and the bread. The misses were the fact they ran out of their specialty prime rib, wilted salad, cold fries, and an average blooming onion. text: I think it says a lot about Edmonton that places like Oil City Roadhouse/Vinyl are closing down and places like GoGo Lounge are popping up. I had a really fun time when my friends and I went here on a Saturday earlier this month (would've written the review sooner but nobody had created the business page here in Yelp yet, and I was too busy then to do it myself). First big plus - atmosphere. The decor is retro-tasteful, with cherry lamps, stools with shapely women legs, cocktail menus on vinyl and a blown-up piece of Edmonton skyline out on the back wall (but with other famous structures across the world strategically inserted here and there). The music the DJ plays is fun, danceable, and familiar. This is a place where you take your closest friends, have a drink (or fifteen), dance where you stand, and HAVE FUN. And when you're ready to have even more fun, you go to the back, try to fit into the photo booth and see if you can bottle the night up in that little strip of awesome. It's pretty cool. Second big plus - selection of cocktails. $12 each, but worth every single buck. They taste marvelous (and are quite strong)! They also have these zodiac shots at ridiculously low prices (I think it came down to $2 per shot) - those taste pretty great too! When we went here last September long weekend, they didn't serve food yet, but I hear that's coming soon (if it hasn't already). I think that could only be a welcome addition to the so-far limited but respectable menu. I personally have no complaints on the palate end of things. Third big plus - no cover, older crowd. Definitely a breath of fresh air after the usual stifling selection of clubs and bars in the city (with overpriced covers or a typically younger clientele). I've never been to the GoGo Lounge location in Montreal myself, but I've heard good things. If this is what this little gem strives to be, then I'm all for it! So to sum up, it's an intimate lounge - great atmosphere, weird retro but tasteful decor, good music, great cocktail selection, no cover, older crowd. And photo booth. Oh yeah, and very interesting washrooms. Now if only we could get one in Calgary...

It took nearly 45 minutes for our appetizer to come out, during which time we'd finished our first round, and had to wait 15 minutes to order a second round. Once the chips came out, they were delicious, as usual. Unfortunately, we then had to wait another half hour for our meals to come out. We were debating whether or not to get up and leave once the food finally arrived. My pork sandwich was phenomenal. I mean, just great. I'd order that again in a second, and cut you if you got near it. My wife's pesto chicken sandwich? Not so much. The chicken was very thinly pounded, and probably the driest chicken I'd ever tasted. It was smothered in mayo, with lettuce and tomato on top, and get this - HAD NO PESTO ON IT! I wasn't in the mood to argue with anyone, so we just dropped our debit card as soon as the food came out, ate as quickly as we could, and got the hell out of there. Honestly, after this experience, and the experience of a friend of ours a couple weeks ago, I'll think twice about High Street. Maybe John will turn it around, but I won't be going back for some time.
label: NEG

text: Soooooooooooooo thankful we found this place. It was our last night in NOLA and our plans changed because Essence Fest pretty much took over the Quarter. So, we stayed in the Garden District and walked to Magazine St, not too far from our hotel. Our goal during our trip was to search out all of the authentic New Orleans cuisine we could. When we got to Magazine St we couldn't find any place that screamed NOLA! Oh no! What were we to do?! After consulting our trusty Yelp apps, we walked past several spots and finally chose Salu -- what a great surprise! While not a NOLA-inspired menu, the menu here was vast with a smart variety of food for all palates. Because our livers weren't damaged enough yet, we ordered a couple of rounds of mojitos and caipirinhas (you know that Brazilian drink that tastes like tequila?). The classic drinks were only $5 each. Hellllooooo! I'll take one or two or three of those! Besides a good and inexpensive drink menu and GREAT food, we experienced some of the best service (though service all over NOLA was exceptional, for the most part). Our server was conversational and gave us suggestions on other really good restaurants for our next trip. In fact, she made a list and gave it to us. She also told us which bars she recommended in the area that were in walking distance from our Garden District hotel since we wanted to steer clear of the French Quarter. We felt like we made a local friend here. Thank you for good food, good drinks, and good conversation!
label: POS

text: Tennou is definitely the BEST sushi place on the west bank! I've been coming here for years and am still satisfied with the food as the recession plays out. My boyfriend and I always get the beef tataki bc it is the best we ever tried. They give a generous portion compared to other sushi places and cut it thin the way it should be. It's also seared to the right temperature and the ponzu sauce goes well with it. Other places usually cook it too much and it usually is very bland elsewhere. And I LOVE the onions that go with it. My favorite rolls are the tennou II roll and salmon naruto. The sexiest man alive roll and hawaiian roll are pretty good also. My favorite salad is the tennou special salad (no whitefish and add avocado and cucumber!) Dessert-wise, the tempera cheesecake is THE BEST here. I've tried many other places like sake, rock n sake, etc. and its just not as good. The mango sorbet and red bean ice cream are also very good here! Service is usually good. The only downfall is that they sometimes charge for unnecessary things. For example, the charged me $1.00 to take out whitefish from the tennou special salad which is ridiculous! Other than that, I still love tennou over other sushi places on the westbank!
label: POS

text: Absolutely Disgusting! Do NOT stay here! Erroneous charges WILL BE charged on your credit card! Report any smell when you check in the front desk...but do so in writing! The rooms absolutely stink, and they will charge you a "Smoking Fee!" saying it was you that left the stench! Save your written complaint- as you will need it to dispute the charges with the management (which is horrible)...so my best advice to anyone thinking of staying here....DO NOT STAY HERE!

text: Ate here last May (2011) when the line for a muffuletta next door was too long. While our waiter was attentive and friendly, the food was awful. The food additionally was pricy. I can only guess this place stays in business from one-time, unsuspecting tourists.

text: It's been sad/weird that the St. Louis area SEVERELY lacks mom & pop coffee places. Kaldi's seems to be one of the only local places I've found. That being said, Kaldi's doesn't just get 5 stars by default of selection, but because they do some great things! The atmosphere at this location is nice with lots of places to sit and spend a few hours working. Outlets are really only found in two locations, near the couches and by the tall chairs. I normally go between 12pm to about 2 or 3 pm in the afternoon. I only ever really compete with moms for places to sit. I went once around 6pm at night to find it full of high school and college students. Quite a different vibe, but it was still nice. They have a GREAT healthy, local, sustainable selection of dishes to eat and baked yummies to munch on. Not to mention, they clearly know their coffee. :)

text: Great brunch! One of the few places in the neighborhood that serves a great breakfast past noon. Food is good, and priced accordingly, and the service is on par as well. This is the only reason that I didn't give it 5 stars. I've never met the woman, but was floored by her rudeness... Anywho, the food and service are fantastic. The live band in the middle of the bar on Saturday brunch is a but much, but enough Bloody Mary's and you don't even mind.

text: Alright, on the count of 3, say, "KIM CHEESE!!" I had the opportunity to check out Kim Cheese today on its opening day, and I have to say that I'm glad I was able to. For those who don't know, it is an Asian fusion type restaurant with Korean BBQ meat tacos. The dine-in area is nice and quaint, but remember that it is a fast-food feel, not a sitdown place with waiters, etc. The items that caught my eye were the beef and spicy pork, either in a group of 3 tacos or a big burrito. I opted for the 3 beef taco combo. When my order was called, my mouth began to water as I saw three Korean BBQ beef tacos (they didn't skimp out on the meat, which is great), filled with fresh veggies. The taste didn't disappoint either, as I thoroughly enjoyed each and every bite. There are a few other items that were interesting, but I'll have to go back and give it a try, namely the Kim Chi Burger, which has a traditional Korean side (Kim Chi) within a beef (korean-bbq-beef) burger. I'll definitely be back! If you are looking for a new place to try out, Kim Cheese is definitely worth a look.

text: It seems I've been hitting up a lot of breakfast places lately. It's been hard to draw me away from the Lincoln Square Pancake House on 56th and Emerson, but the rave reviews for Keystone Deli managed it. I'll be mixing that one in frequently, as it's terrific also. So when I needed a brunch on Saturday, I thought I'd try out the Original Pancake House. In a word: Disappointing. I felt pretty jammed in here among large tables and it was really loud. Everything seemed very cramped and the lack of carpet or other sound dampeners meant everything just echoed, forcing people to talk louder, which only exacerbated the problem. This was not a relaxing experience. Then I opened the menu. I couldn't believe the prices! These breakfast foods must be baked with gold because it seemed incredibly expensive to me, especially after my recent experiences at other places. $8 for pancakes with no sides? $4+ for a side of bacon? You've got to be kidding me. To make matters worse, there were very few combo options. So if you simply wanted some pancakes and bacon, you were paying $12-$13 with nothing else offered. Contrast this with a recent meal at the Keystone Deli, where I had pancakes, 2 eggs, smoked sausage, and potatoes (all large portions) for around $7-8 total. Oh, and the food at the Deli was vastly superior to the OPH. So how was the food? My pancakes were acceptable but not special. The bacon was cut very thick, not very crispy, and seemed soaked with grease. It was almost like it had not been hot enough during cooking or that the bacon was so thick that it soaked up all the grease. I didn't enjoy it. I'll be avoiding OPH in the future. However, judging from the overflow crowd, it seems I may be the only one who feels this way.

text: It's consistent. It's delicious. They make a fuss about special occasions. The service is always great. I've been here a few times, the most recent was for Anniversary Lunch. Forever a Pasta St. Charles fan, I was in the mood to try something different, which led me to ask about the soup du jour. The waiter told me it was an oyster corn soup, but that he wouldn't let me order it, because the soup was something new that turned our somewhat questionable. I applauded him on his honesty, and then as Husband and I grew more curious, he offered to bring us samples. It was pretty terrible, reminding us of the flavor that water might have after crawfish were purged in it, but we can't say he didn't warn us! The waiter also brought us little smoked salmon bruschetta with herbed cream cheese, which were delicious. Bread man kept us full of French Bread, too. On to what we actually ordered: We got the Crabmeat Cheesecake to share. I've tasted it before and wasn't impressed. Wasn't impressed when Husband ordered it, either. The crust tasted a little burnt and it seemed really dry. Husband got the oyster salad entree and I got the Pasta St. Charles. Although I generally steer clear of cream based sauces when I dine out, this one is worth the damage to my waistline. Husband's oysters were tasty, too; much better than the counterpart salad at their sister, Bourbon House. More bread. I ordered bread pudding, which was delivered on an enormous plate with a large slab of Mississippi Mud Pie, with "Happy Anniversary" written in chocolate. I wasn't a big fan of the bread pudding (the bananas foster is a better choice), but the Mud Pie was delicious. Didn't think we had any room, but there wasn't a bite of dessert left. It's consistent, it's delicious. They make a fuss. Which makes us come back.

text: This is hands down the best Mexican food I have ever had! My boyfriend and I were walking along state street when we happened upon this two-month old restaurant, we read the yelp reviews and decided to give it a shot. The wait without a reservation on a Saturday night was 45 minutes and we were happy to wait at a cocktail table and drink for 45 minutes, but after one drink and only 10 minutes we were seated. It is a Mexican tapas bar which I have never come across before, and it is such a welcome change to the typically large American/Mexican portions. We ordered 4 Tapas and an appetizer and we were blown away by each and every one. What we ordered: Japanese Oysters - WOW! Small, delicate oysters with a wonderful chimi churri inspired cocktail sauce Shrimp and Crab Empanadas - I am not usually a seafood lover but these empanadas blew my mind Chicken Tastatidos - The cutest little bite size tostadas with the most savory spicy marinated chicken I have ever had Cheese Tamale - Made in house and steamed to order - it literally melted in my mouth Short Rib Corn Cakes - By far the best dish of the night! The most tender, juicy short rib on home-made corn cakes, it doesn't get better than this. Cocktails: My boyfriend got a tequila flight while I consumed a house margarita which was authentic and simple. They do not make blended or flavored margaritas which I really respect. When I wanted to switch it up, I ordered the Stoli, blackberry and basil drink and it is one of the best drinks I have ever tried in my life (and I like to drink). The decor and service were both 5 stars. I love this spot, I highly recommend it and will be returning as often as possible.

text: This is one of my new favorite spots! We've been twice now and had a great experience both times. The first time I got the grass fed burger, and it was PERFECT. The black bean salad that accompanied it was fresh and packed with flavor. The meals everyone else in my family got were all delicious, too! All of the seating is outside, but there's always a breeze and we were very comfortable. The second time we went, it was late at night and they had excellent live music. The atmosphere was like one big party! The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 was because the BBQ pork sandwich I got on my second visit was OK but not as mind-blowing as the burger I had previously. The sweet potato fries were AMAZING ... if you go, I definitely recommend ordering a couple of plates because they will disappear quickly! If we move to Safety Harbor like we hope to, we will definitely be Whistle Stop regulars! :)

text: Okay, so this place is essentially a mainstay in Rittenhouse square. I almost feel like I don't need to review La Colombe, as everyone is aware of its existence. I used to go to La Colombe often, before I saw the light of what actual quality coffee tasted like. So I have this complex opinion about La Colombe, but I think I've kind of seen the light for what it is. First off, yes it's inexpensive relatively for okay coffee. But you're trading off the fact that you're not getting great coffee. The coffee itself is nothing to write home about. I'd go without it. The espresso is good, I usually get a double macchiato or a cappuccino when I go there. I'd say that the place is fairly mechanical, and it will give you the same thing on a consistent basis. Speaking of consistency, you will always find yourself with a long line and seating is at a premium. You'll find a lot of couples who will be ravenous in the line, send one person to get a seat, while the other waits in line. This is the name of the game, as no one is really respectful enough to wait in line together. There's a tendency for haughty privileged middle-aged couple to boast about their 401k's loudly in front of you in hope of you hearing how successful their meaningless life is. text: For some reason, this restaurant reminds me of 'The Cheesecake Factory'. I mean, the menu reads the same, I think some of the dishes are similar and hell, both sell a crazy variety of cheesecake. I just wanted to point that out because I've felt that way for years. Odd similarities. Anyway, I've dined in this place SEVERAL times since 2005, when I first came here with my ex. Each time, there was always something weird going, either inside the restaurant or just outside the door. More on that later. This last time, I came in with some friends from Pensacola. Why on Earth they decided to dine at a chain restaurant for their first visit to New Orleans is beyond me. Have you ever wondered what the deal is with that? New Orleans is unique right down to the core, from the eclectic mix of individuals to the cuisine to the architecture. Why travel hundreds and sometimes, thousands of miles to eat at a chain restaurant that you can experience anywhere. Why not actually try something that's bred in the city you're visiting and remains only local. Does McDonald's in Atlanta taste any better than McDonald's in Texas? No, because it's friggin' McDonald's. In any case, this is what they wanted and so we decided to dine. As usual, while the hostess seated us immediately and was courteous, it took quite a while before we got a waiter. 10 minutes must have passed before we flagged someone down to find our server. Eventually some guy stumbled from the bar area to take our order. At first, we only ordered drinks and mine was a simple Jack Daniels and Coke. That's typically my weapon of choice, for those who don't know me well yet. The drinks took a VERY long time to arrive. Finally, they showed up and my friend's wife got the wrong wine. The waiter argued with us, explaining that we were wrong. The wine wasn't even the proper color. He finally went to the back and brought out what she had ordered. For the sake of keeping this review within the 5,000 character limit, I am only reviewing MY order. I placed a request for the Lemon Garlic Chicken with Rosemary Glaze and it came with garlic mashed potatoes. The food arrived promptly this time so no complaints there. My chicken, however, was EXTREMELY salty. I was surprised that the intense amount of salt content didn't dry out the bird. I then sampled the mashed potatoes and they, too, were overly salty. It took me almost 4 Jack & Cokes to rinse away the sodium. I also want to add that in all the times I have been frequenting this establishment, my entrees have either been too salty or too bland. Wait staff are not very attentive at all, especially when it gets later in the evening and there's usually a raucous going on inside or outside the joint. Allow me to explain.... The last three times that I've dined at this location, the police have been there and it's never on pleasant terms. On this last visit, my party and I walked up the sidewalk and two cop cars were parked nose-to-nose in front of the doors. When we walked in, our eyes immediately started burning and our noses running. It was from a cloud of pepper spray in the area. What the hell was going on?? I immediately ran to the restroom, where 3 women were seated on the bench just outside. Two of them were arguing very loudly and suddenly, they began exchanging blows. It appeared as if they had already had an altercation once earlier that evening. One of the women's dresses was ripped at the shoulder, exposing her bra. The other girl was laying face down on the bench. Another girl had a badly bruised eye and was covering it with a pack of ice. Another woman had scratches on her face and down her arm, clothes ripped. As soon as the two women began throwing punches, two cops rushed in immediately and grabbed the women. Someone fired off another round of pepper spray but I could not tell where it originated from. After I cleaned up in the bathroom and came back out, one of the women was missing and the others were in handcuffs. I saw what I presumed to be the manager near the entrance speaking to police, his hair disheveled and shirt wrinkled and un-tucked. Later, our waiter explained that the women engaged in a boxing match inside the restaurant when one of them was caught dining with the other's boyfriend. Punches were exchanged, the manager jumped into the fray, customers fled and the cops were called. Again, I'm just reiterating what the waiter told us. This is not the only time I've dined here where cops were called in. I'm going to close with this: The food is okay. That's all. There are better places to dine, in my opinion, especially if you're in the Uptown area. This restaurant is too streaky, suffers from poor wait staff, under-seasoned or over-seasoned dishes and seems to be a prime location for physical altercations. I'd pass on this one and you should, too!

It wasn't trying to pretend it was healthy, and it was effectively comfort food. It was pretty large, too, and I was able to save half for dinner the next day. It held up! A caveat: both the chicken and the cheese are soy-based. They had good texture, and the cheese was surprisingly creamygooey*, so I'm not suggesting a total overhaul. Just maybe experiment in the kitchen with some seitan or nut cheese and see what happens. I don't get fussy about some soy here or there (it's certainly better than its animal counterparts), but diversity is awesome. And less likely to kill us. I loved the atmosphere of the take-out section, totally chill and not fancy at all. I could've been in any meat-serving joint in the city, and I wouldn't have noticed the difference, besides the menu. The service was great - pleasant, but genuine. The prices are more than fair, especially considering I made two meals out of one sandwich. I will definitely be back, I'll just make sure not to eat anything with soy for the preceding and following 24 hours. *no casein, though, in case you were wondering. All of the sandwiches come with Giardia (the Italian vegetable salad) in them. It was an usual addition. I liked it on the beef gyro, not so sure on falafal. I tried the beef gyro as recommended to me. It was ok. There are many better Gyros around. However, the hot and spicy falafel is da bomb! The addition of the red pepper sauce adds just enough zing to make this pepperhead really appreciate this sandwich! I also like the Cornichon and the Italian veggie salad. The only knock I have is the Falafel themselves are a little moister than I like, and it is magnified by the other ingredients. But again it is really spectacular! I also had the Baba Ghanouj. It was good. The cornichions in this are perfect. Tart and crunchy. I liked the fresh made Pitas that came with it. It is a medium size strip mall restaurant. That has a very small selection of dried goods to take home. Which looks like it includes the pepper sauce and the italian vegetable mix is included in the selection. They call themselves a bakery but I only saw Pitas and a few (2-3) types of sweet pastries.

text: I started with the Morimoto Sashimi. The request to replace any shellfish with an alternative to accommodate an allergy was declined at it was against the chef's vision (forget about being against anaphylaxis, but hey), but the crab could at least be placed on another plate. For the price, you don't get a lot of fish (2 pieces of 4 fish and 1 crab), but they are incredibly fresh, which makes it worth the splurge. I picked Duck Duck Duck for my entree. The duck breast is amazing (the skin was fantastically crispy and tasty); the confit fried rice was delicious (I usually hate fried rice, but this is a different dish all together); and the runny duck egg was rich and soaked nicely into the rice. We finished with the Yuzu Meringue Tart, which was like a lemon meringue. The fresh mango provided a sweet balance, and overall the dessert was light enough that you should opt for it, even if you're stuffed full of other good food.

text: My significant other and I have been South Street fans for many years. Always one of our "go to" places for tasty food, good atmosphere and cocktails on a sunny afternoon. One of my big pet peeves is core pieces in a salad. This is the part that I would toss in the trash at home. This salad was completely white and yellow pieces of "lettuce" hidden under mounds of cheese and cucumber. Not a green piece of lettuce in sight. Think the cheese and cucumber was supposed to cover up the nasty lettuce. We both ordered the pulled pork plate which used to be served over a crispy cornbread pancake. The pork was the best thing on the plates and it was even mediocre. My baked beans were served cold with way too many chunks of scallions in them. The tater tots that were usually the highlight of the meal were undercooked and lacked that creamy inside to crispy outside ratio that we've always loved. What happened to our South Street? Extremely diappointed and will have to change our "go to" lists of Nashville standard restaurants, mainly removing South Street. So sad :(

text: There is something somewhat horrifying about the ubiquitous (look up that word, Jay!) heavy, brown glutinous (another word for Jay to look up) sauce that drowns so many Chinese dishes, so I tend to stay away from Chinese restaurants in general. Cold and rainy kind of day, so I was craving some war won ton soup. It was okay, but it could have had a deeper flavored broth, though it was generous enough with five won tons and a nice handful of nice sized shrimp. For $6.50, it was a huge bowl, so I saved most of it to take home. (Back in the mountains the next day, I took the leftovers, added a little more chicken broth, a dash of fish sauce, and heated it up with some simple glass noodles - now it was officially delicious.) I scanned the menu, consciously trying to avoid any dish that might have the dreaded brown sauce. I chose the simple sounding "barbecued pork and rice" dish, imagining something closer to what Vietnamese grilled pork is like - thin slices of pork with nice charring and crispity edges. Instead, what I got was a giant mound of rice with a few sliced pieces of pork (the same sliced pieces of pork that was floating in my soup) and a few vegetables drowning in THE DREADED BROWN SAUCE. Epic, epic, fail.

text: It kind of saddens me to write this review. My husband and I used to be Blue Ocean enthusiasts. We were regular customers for Sunday lunch when they had AYCE at their former location. The atmosphere used to be great, the servers were friendly, and the sushi was delicious. Then Blue Ocean discontinued their AYCE on weekends (Note: they have changed back to AYCE on weekends) and they moved to a new location. Sometime during that transition the hubby and I began to branch out and try other sushi restaurants. We made the trek to Sushi Ai on Dorsett and really enjoyed it - it had fewer "crazy" options but great, tasty sushi. Over time Blue Ocean sort of lost its charm. Every few months we went back to Blue Ocean to get some of the items that they made best: crag rangoons, squid salad, and funky rolls. They were good, but not as good as before. After a 3-4 month hiatus, we went back to Blue Ocean today. I was somewhat disappointed. The sushi was so-so and one of the rolls had a strange, fishy taste (as if it were not quite fresh). The AYCE tier prices have increased slightly and the squid salad is no longer included. There were other minor issues including a freezing cold restaurant, a decent wait time, and an underenthused staff. Overall, it was okay but not a great meal. I think Sushi Ai is our staple sushi restaurant from now on. For the record, I really wanted to love Blue Ocean today but it just didn't happen. Bring back the old vibe!!

text: I don't really want to let the secret out... But I honestly was allowed to have a taste of ALL of the Jeni's ice cream flavors available at Hot & Cold. And they were all really, really good. Hot & Cold is less like Starbucks (fun flavors and novelty drinks!) and more like Nashville's local and loved Crema (ALL ABOUT ESPRESSO). I wouldn't call myself a coffee connoisseur by ANY means, but the soy cafe au lait with mocha (I know you're laughing) I had at Hot & Cold tasted robust and un-chocolatey, an un-sweetness I've come to identity with an actually well made coffee drink. The store is offering a nice selection of also local and loved Las Paletas Mexican popsicles, even offering a mini-paleta called a Chiquita. Aww, how cute. But if size matters to you! - there's a Ben & Jerry's Vermonster-like sundae available (Lord knows who's ordering this... except me on my birthday later this year...or maybe just next week...) that combines four scoops of ice cream, four chiquitas, and other STUFF. Yum. Really, that Jeni's ice cream is a seriously great find. It's definitely an all flavor, no crap-ingredients product. It's being sold by the pint in the store as well, for $10. Yeah, that's a lot.. but it's a hell of a product and Hot & Cold needs to make a profit too! The two young guys working behind the counter seemed really enthusiastic about all of Hot & Cold's offerings. Not only did I sample 5-6 ice cream flavors, I could have smelled the tea leaves if I'd wanted to! I don't know if those guys are big foodies, or they love coffee, or they're just glad to have a job! Any of the above. I'll see them again, for sure.

text: Before submitting this review, I briefly skimmed the notes of previous reviewers. Based on my experiences here, I'd agree on one thing: This place is a mixed bag. Before even entering the restaurant, I have to say that even the architectural design is confusing. What are there, like 3 floors?? Is this place THAT busy? What's up there? I've never been up there and no one seems to know what it's for. When I got to the front door, I noticed a valet booth and a couple of young men trading banter outside. This place has a valet?? Well, I don't want to get off on a rant too soon in this review so let me continue on. Inside, my friend and I stood for some time by the front entrance, waiting to be seated. I saw waiters and waitresses seemingly milling around but not really doing much at all. There was no hostess to be seen. After someone called from the back, a girl arrived to seat us. I think the exterior of this building is pretty sleek and maintains a modern flair, as does the interior. The ceiling has a very industrial feel to it with exposed pipes, air shafts and vents twisting over one another, headed this way and that. The furnishings themselves reminded me a hotel, though. I can't exactly explain why. The color scheme utilizes a lot of muddled down browns, blues and reds; very earthy tones. It was clean enough but I wasn't sure what vibe the owner was trying to create. When I reviewed the menu, I found the prices quite high for the offerings. Most of the dishes were what I would consider pretty classic Chinese dishes: chicken and vegetables, General Tsao's chicken, Kung Pao, Moo Goo Gai Pan, Mongolian Beef, etc. Typically, I find these dishes at a Chinese take-out joint for $6 to $7 . These dishes were all about $15. We were so hungry that we immediately placed an order. I put in an order for the Mongolian Beef at $14. There was no mention of a side of rice so I asked the waitress about rice. She stated that rice came with the order. Now, for some time, I waited for the order. I heard cooks in the background banging around, dishes crashing; the sounds of a furious food station cranking out delicious, hot, fresh meals. At the point that I was just about to ask the waitress where our food was, she arrived with the food tray and proceeded to hand us our dishes. She placed the Mongolian Beef platter before me and asked if that was all. I replied no, that the side of rice was missing. 5 minutes later, she returned and said it would be an extra charge. For rice?? In a Chinese restaurant?? Rice is like, one of the cheapest foods and typically, an Asian restaurant gives you rice whether you want it or not. For $15, I believe rice should be included. I explained this to the waitress and she left again. Later, she returned and said that while they do charge for rice, the chef allowed me a dish of rice this time. The waitress, again returned with a dish of fried rice. I took one bite of it and had to spit it out. It tasted like fiberglass! In addition, it was completely burned and dried out. After some time, the waitress came by to bring us the check and asked us how the food was. I explained that the rice was burned and dried. It absolutely felt like I was trying to eat glass. She mumbled something and went back to the food station, never to return again. Ok, let me sum up my thoughts. First of all, let's review the history of the joint. The restaurant is owned by Steve Ho, who was a former partner at 'Five Happiness' and had sold his shares in the restaurant shortly before Hurricane Katrina to open Hoshun. While Ho admits that the restaurant is a fusion of Chinese, Thai and Vietnamese cuisines, I'm confused as to what type of direction this restaurant was/is intended to go. The prices clearly suggest an upscale environment, as does the valet outside on the curb. To expound on this, why does the restaurant even have a valet?? Are they trying to attract wealthy customers? If that's the case, wealthy guests will know if it's truly a classy joint or not - and this place is NOT. While there are a few fusion dishes available on the menu, the presentation and flavor are average, at best. I didn't experience anything different here than I would in a hole-in-the-wall late night Chinese take-out. As a matter of fact, I've actually had BETTER Chinese food in some buffets. That's quite sad. To top it off, they tried to charge me for rice, which clearly should have come with the meal. If that wasn't enough, it was dried out, old and burned. Any restaurant, especially Asian, that cannot properly cook rice immediately gets a cross through their name in my book. In writing this review, I've not been able to locate a single accolade of the establishment since 2008, which is when they first opened, and I imagine that was ONLY because they were new. Hopefully, Hoshun can pull it together. New Orleans lacks a solid Chinese gourmet outside 'Five Happiness'

text: I read another review of Sun King that said, "I am not a beer connoisseur". Well, I am and I have to say that their beer is pretty bad. Even on a local level and not compared to a national audience, their beer is bad. There are consistent off flavors throughout their brews that make me think they use the same strain of yeast throughout their brews. At the very least, they run their cultures for too many generations. I also notice some residual sweetness and slight banana flavor in some of their brews that is consistent with a high temperature fermentation. The Osiris is either overhopped or undermalted, you can look at it either way. It is unbalanced though. It has the hoppiness of an IPA and is as light on the malt as a Pale. Their Cream Ale is a classic case in point that it is actually harder to make a light beer that is balanced and without off flavors, they have proven that by all of the off-flavors that come through on their light brew. It may be good as a transitional beer when going from "fizzy yellow water" domestics beers, but a person will soon graduate. The Wee Mac is just......gross. Disgustingly gross, horrible off flavors. When I first tried it I thought that a bad batch had gotten through QC. A few months later I gave it another go and apparently that is how it is supposed to taste? The dry irish stout, although the abv is within style guidelines, tastes hot. Once again, there are awful flavors that come through upon tasting. Blech. Popcorn Pilsner? I am all for experimental but this beer just tastes like shit. I couldn't even choke down the little tasting cup. Cream Dream, the malt profile of their cream ale with a lot more hop. Baaaad idea. If a person were to come up with a textbook example of how to make an unbalanced beer, this would be it. Imagine Miller Lite with a crapload of hops. Yes, it is that bad. Their Black IPA.......I have run out of unique ways to describe their beers. It is shit. Imagine a double Guinness with a lot of hop. Yes, it is that bad. Malus Pi, what idea got rejected in favor of making a Wit with oats and crabapples? Seriously, in what brainstorming session was there an idea worse than this? Did someone propose brewing a beer with human excrement? All in all, I really dislike everything they have produced. I have no idea how they have remained in business. I am done giving them an honest try. When someone asks if I would like a Sun King beer, I answer honestly that I would rather drink urine. I will however give them credit for being at the forefront of the craft beer movement here in Indianapolis. They did not start it, it would have happened without them. I suppose it does show the power of being first to market though. If you are the first, you can have a shitty product and still be a success. Addendum: They claim that they put their beer in cans because it is better for the beer. That is BS. Can and canning lines are cheaper than bottling lines. That is the only reason. Cans are a far inferior way of packaging beer. They want us to think of it as a miniature keg for your beer......then why do they keg in HDPE kegs? Also, old school kegs are stainless steel. They are not stainless steel because it is the ideal material to package beer in, they are stainless because it is durable and easy to clean. Glass has always been and will always be a better container for beer than aluminum cans. Don't fall for the hype and marketing and buy a good beer in a bottle. Also, please tell me they have stopped the "we don't fill growlers from other breweries" BS. Everyone else does it. Just slap a sticker on it and get over yourselves. You are making money on the beer that goes in the growler, not on the growler itself. As soon as I learned about that I put all the growlers that friends had given me or left behind (that we had filled with beer from other local breweries) and put them in the recycling bin.

After some quick discussion we decide that we're most likely not to get rejected at The Palm. I mean they have cartoons all over the walls, they'll tolerate jeans and polo shirts, right? Figuring it's our best chance we head to the Palm. Just as anticipated they welcome us in without hesitation and even better we're not the most dressed down group there. We're seated right away and our waiter, Gabriel, is there instantly. We're ordering drinks and he's running down specials. When he leaves to let us digest the menu, that's when the dilemma sets in. We're Catholics in a Steakhouse on Good Friday. Running through the options I'm conflicted, on one hand I've been good all Lent and here I am at the last meal on the last day on the other hand if I'm spending that much on dinner I should get what I want, and I love steak. Gabriel returns to take our order and starts around the table, my dining partners go crab-cake, crab-cake, tuna and now it's to me. I'm thinking fish but then come to my senses, I mean there are plenty of reasons I'm going to burn, I doubt a steak is going to be the tipping point. NY Strip it is. My steak came out and it was cooked perfectly and was very good but not great. With the competition all around them they need to be serving 5s, this steak was a 4. Perhaps it was just God mad at me ... The mashed potatoes and au gratin potatoes were both pretty good as well. But again they need to be serving 5s and these were both 4s. text: Time for a downgrade to 2 stars. My mother was visiting from Canada, and requested that on this visit, she wanted to try beignets. Knowing that Joe's is right down the street from us, I figured this was a better alternative in the extreme heat than going down to the super touristy Cafe Du Monde. This was our breakfast stop on Saturday morning. We ordered a little bit of actual food, and then one order of beignets to share at the table. Actually, let me backtrack a little... we came in, and instinctivly went to the counter to order, like one would expect at a coffee/donut shop. They told us to sit down if we were dining in. I figured, ok, great, they have waiter service.. even better! After about 7 minutes of waiting, they took our drink order. They were out of apple juice so we got 3 orange juices and I ordered a cafe au lait (after all, that's required with beignets in my mind). The OJ came quickly. The cafe au lait somehow took 10 minutes to make. I was almost ready to scratch the "au lait" and just ask for a regular coffee, but couldn't find the waitress anywhere until the cafe au lait finally arrived. It was okay, but I've had better just about everywhere. Definitely not worth the wait. My fiance enjoyed his donuts. The beignets were excellent. The waffle that my mother and my toddler split was exceptionally subpar. It arrived lukewarm at best. My omelet... ugh. I ordered it with cheddar cheese, as you apparently have the choice of cheddar or american. I HATE processed fake slimy cheese. When it finally arrived, it had 2 slices of american on top. Luckily, they weren't melted at all, so I just picked those off and tossed them to the side of the plate. No cheese for me. Next I discovered the lovely canned mushrooms inside of the omelet. The sausage and bell peppers were seemingly fresh. The egg itself was coated in so much butter that I couldn't taste anything but butter anyway though. I ate half of it and gave it to the fiance to finish, as the pool of butter on the plate was a major turn off. At the end of it all, the waitress never came by to collect our payment for the food, so we went to the counter to pay - despite being told not to order at the counter in the first place. Would I come back to Joe's? Sure, but only for beignets, which will not be a frequent trip. I haven't found anything else worthy of the exceptional wait time that has apparently become the norm at this establishment.

text: Brad Pitt says, "I want to see a world where there are more churches on corners than Seven-Elevens." Jon A says, "I want more taquerias on corners than Liquor Stores." Do you ever find yourself turning around in a parking lot, or pulling over to take a phone call, then when you look up, or turn the corner you just really want *poof* a taqueria to be right where you're heading? I do. And today... that happened. *Warning: Tangential justification of taquerias over churches.* Brad Pitt has a point about churches & 7/11s, yes, & more power to him... but there's also an epidemic of liquor stores on corners in certain neighborhoods to deal with. Typically these liquor stores offer payday advances (to take advantage of those that aren't able to open a checking account) and are owned by someone who lives in the burbs (I've met the owner of over 20 stores: he lives in Franklin, IN and owns stores throughout neighborhoods he won't go to). At any rate... an answer to not having liquor stores... have successful neighborhood owned taquerias on corners that would normally have these. Taquerias / Carnicerias are a positive, safe environment for the community to congregate. They're also going to attract safe, interested people from outside the neighborhood (read: me). *End of tangent.* This corner... 38th & High School could easily have a liquor store. Instead, outside of a Home Depot, in the parking lot, there's this taco shack (sort of tucked behind a dairy queen). There were fathers & sons & others lingering drinking sodas from bottles. There are a couple picnic tables you can sit at outside. It's a 12x12 shack and half of it is where you enter & order. There's a bar that seats 4. Annnnnnd.... they have Suadero! Every time I go to a taqueria I ask for Suadero and every time I'm bummed as they don't have it. Demetrio has it. Suadero is brisket -- the fatty side of brisket, and it's delicious. It's been a long 3 years since I've had suadero.This was the best taco I've had in Indianapolis. The tacos are $2 and of the super taco sort. I'm going to make excuses to work on the West Side so I can be here more. Or if I feel like a late night drive out of downtown... as they're open 'til midnight on the weekends. *Cash Only* Yes there's a successful trend of truffle-oiled, pancetta paella, korean burrito food trucks happening in Indy. There's something else happening: there are incredible authentic taquerias everywhere. I traveled the country for two years so I could find these. Now they're all right here.

In most places "vegan" and "vegetarian" constitutes an automatic redonkulous "status upcharge" but yet you can buy a vegan muffin or giant cookie for under $2 and add vegan sausage to your wrap for 50 cents. It almost makes parenting seem a lot less suffocating and if there were more accommodating, kid-friendly places like this in the country then maybe I'd consider having one.
