text: Birthday dinner review! Kevin Sbraga has been one of the very few Top Chef finalists to win it all that I've actually cheered on to do so! So as the restaurant opened, the solid reviews kept pouring in, and Adam Erace (http://www.citypaper.net/food/2011-12-15-kevin-sbraga-philadelphia-review.html?c=r) and Brian Freedman (http://www.philadelphiaweekly.com/food/reviews/Kevin-Sbraga-Top-Chef-Broad-Street.html) painted pictures of culinary excellence with their articles; I knew that I was destined to use my birthday dinner as the chance to finally savor it for myself. And, with what another kitchen wizard who needs little introduction on here dished out for me last year coming in first (http://www.yelp.com/biz/sycamore-lansdowne), This might just be the 2nd best birthday meal that I've ever had! When you're eating at Top Chef winners restaurant you expect to have an incredible experience that leads to incredible food. But what I liked about Sbraga was the fact that you got one of those without it being cocky in the process. Throughout the evening you could catch glimpses of Kevin holding it down in the kitchen with his crew, or checking in on his front of house. And through those glimpses you could definitely see someone who truly loved what he was doing, and didn't put himself above anyone else on his team because he won a TV Show. And that projected onto a team who delivered some of the best service possible! Whether you go with the Prix Fixe 4 course for $45, or the special Chef's Tasting meal that features whatever Sbraga prepares on the spot, you're treated to a real celebration of culinary perfection. Even more so if you go with the beverage pairings, although the Sbraga Punch and Coffee Stout from Williamsburg Alewerks suited me perfectly. The Foie Gras Soup was table poured, and its rose petal relish accompaniment featured just a hint of pumpernickel. It was so delicious that I was tempted to lap it out of the bowl! Ever since reading Freedman's article I've been dreaming about the duo of perfectly seared scallop and pork belly. And the beets, cream fraiche, and beet jus that they shared its plate with made it a perfect ballet between sweet and savory. For the main course I just had to get the combo of lamb chop and belly; and it was perfectly aligned with Asian pears and steel cut oats. While ordering an artisanal cheese plate is a dessert tradition that I normally do when its offered, The hot chocolate and Grand Mariner concoction proved to be a decadent and satisfying treat that was too good to pass up! So in the end I walked away satisfied after a perfect meal. And while its still too early to call, Sbraga might just be leaving its mark as best new restaurant of the year!

text: I can't say enough good things about Peter's, and I can't recommend Jessica and Anita highly enough; I'd be willing to take a chance with any of their other staff due to the extremely positive interactions I've experienced time and time again. Definitely check out their website--they offer a HUGE range of services at reasonable prices for the quality of service received. I pay $35 to continuously get the best cuts of my life. To me, that's a great value. (I was paying $50-60 per visit for cuts I wasn't satisfied with after my stylist's departure. That was steep enough for cuts I liked, but totally out of the question for sub-par work.) Their online booking system makes it easy to find an appointment when I need one, and booking at last minute has never been a problem for me. Jessica has been doing my brows for 5 or 6 years now and I will NEVER let anyone else touch my brows (for as long as I can avoid it). She has also done brazilians for me and a few friends. We have had great experiences with her performing this service--she is thorough and makes you feel very comfortable. Although I have found a brazilian service I like for much less elsewhere, I will always return to see Jessica to get my brows done. For years I was getting my haircut by Nancy at Blaze in downtown West Chester, but when she left I decided to give Peter's a shot since I'm in there frequently to get my brows done anyway. BEST thing that has ever happened to my hair!! I see Anita--she's very experienced and just knows exactly how to handle hair. She's fun to talk to about travels and adventures and is always greets me with a big smile. Speaking of smiles, for as long as I've been visiting Peter's, the staff there has always been incredibly friendly and helpful. There was a problem with my payment during the visit before last and the staff was incredibly discrete and helpful in helping me set up arrangements to pay on my next visit. What could have been a very embarrassing moment was quickly turned into a great customer service experience. Although it's hidden away behind Wawa in an unassuming looking building, Peter's has top notch facilities that always put me into a tranquil state. The spa area is beautiful and very nicely kept, and the salon is always pristine and filled with light due to some huge windows. Give them a visit; you won't be sorry!

They guy who served our food wasn't very talkative. I get that a lot of most meat and 3 places. They don't seem to be very friendly. It is what it is. I ordered the ribs, "white beans", turnip greens and mac n cheese. I was so disappointed about the turnip greens. It was missing something but I can't quite put my finger on it. It just tasted funny. The ribs were slightly cold and very fatty, but as far as the taste, it was just ok. I've had better. The "white beans" tastes like everyone elses "white beans" ive ever had, but I was very impressed by the hotwater corn bread and mac and cheese. I've had better food when it comes to a meat and 3. I'm not rushing to make a trip over to Skillet's any time soon, but I'm for certain ill be back someday in the future. I want to try other things and being this place just opened, I can see them getting better and better. If you live or in the the Hermitage area, give it a shot. text: My friend goes to Bangz and loves it, but I haven't had similar experiences. I went in with a damaged haircut. I previously asked someone to do a quick trim for me, and he managed to take out a chunk of uneven hair on one side, nothing on the other. I went to Bangz for a fix... just bring the overall length up about an inch with a nice shape. I usually don't care much about hair--it always grows back, but I left this place to my first tears over a haircut (and after the chunk-cutting debacle, that's saying a lot). The (owner?) of the salon went to town. The only things I specified was 1. nice shape, higher in the back, longer on the sides and 2. please don't touch my bangs, I'm trying to grow them out. Not only did she chop up my bangs, she gave me my first ever mullet. Mullet! I wear glasses and take them off for haircuts, and let me tell you... I'm blind when that happens. I saw a blurry shape, tried to look, couldn't tell and thought it looked nice and left. she had curled up the back of my hair and tucked it under so much that it LOOKED shorter in the back. She had blown out my hair into the rattiest, nastiest texture I have ever seen on my head. I kid you not. It looked filthy, fried, and ratty... and I have healthy, shiny hair. It resembled a helmet or really, really bad hair from the 40s. I tried to wash it out, hoping that maybe she just couldn't style. Instead, there was a literal mullet on my head. I refused to go back to fix it and instead went to another salon to a master stylist (had to bring out the big guns this time). He was as horrified as I was and chopped it off mid-ear all the way around because there was just no saving that scary mess. Visit two. Yes, two. My friend got married and had all of the bridesmaids in for this salon for styling. I went in with a photo of a flapper type wave style and went out with a huge curled mess on my head by the same woman. It looked like a separate entity and she used this weird Bobby pin type thing to hold up one side. Not the type of pin that you pull apart and then slide into hair, so it secures it. The type where the two sides of the pin stick out straight from each other, a few millimeters apart, and never closes. I have fine hair. That crap fell out the moment I left. My hair, for a wedding, fell into a more and more depressive mess throughout the day because the stylist used about one second of hairspray. It went from the original bad to worse. My friend's hair was nice and the hair of some of the other bridesmaids was great, but many of them had hair fall flat and literally just fall out of the style in large pieces throughout the day. The makeup artist didn't match foundation to the bride's neck and got mascara all over her cheeks. All in all, two horrible experiences and I've learned my lesson--there won't be a third.

text: Obviously, there's not much I can say about The Cheesecake Factory, that hasn't already been said. This place is a family favorite, especially for birthdays! Our most recent trip however (25 Jan 12), fell a bit short of what I have come to expect (and love) about TCF. Typically, I'd give TCF a 4-star rating. But on this occasion, 2.5 at best. Let's walk through this chronologically... after being seated, our waiter took our drink order. I asked what kind of single-malt Scotch they had, the waiter was clueless. I asked him to please ask the bartender for a Scoth list. No harm... I ultimately ended up ordering one of my favorites, an Oban. However, it was brought to me in a brandy snifter! Don't like drinks not properly served! The Cheesecake Factory is known for it's liberal appetizers! In most cases, the appetizer is usually enough to satisfy a moderate appetite. I must assume the economy crunch and rising price of food has severely impacted TCF's ability to serve these appetizers, at a moderate price. All of the appetizers we ordered were small quantities/size. No longer a value for the price paid. Just skip the appetizer and go straight to the entree! All of the entrees were fine, not remarkable, but fine. My daughter ordered the Bang-Bang Chicken and Shrimp (her favorite). Unfortunately, half-way though her meal, she found a hair on her plate. Her meal ended there! Now I realize, occasionally, things like this happen in every restaurant. Not that they should, but the plain fact is they do. But the damage is usually mitigated by the staff's response. The waiter immediately brought it to the attention of the manager, who promptly came to the table, apologized, and offered to do whatever was necessary to make it right. That's the response I expect, and that made the occurance less unpleasant. My other daughter, who was celebrating her birthday, had the New Orleans Shrimp. She liked it, but to me, it seemed to be a bit scarce on the shrimp/sausage. This was hidden by an exorbitant amount of white rice (enought to feed the whole family) used to fill in far too much empty space on the plate! My son had the Cajun Jambalaya Pasta and seemed to really enjoy it. I had the Hibachi Steak. Not bad, but way over-priced for the small cut of beef. The shiitake mushroom/bean sprout/onion topping was exceptional, though! It was accompanyed by tempura-battered asparagus. That was incredible. Unfortunately, it only came with two spears. All things considered, our entrees were, well, satisfying. Dinner was rounded out with what else? Cheesecake! I mean why go there and not have cheescake for dessert. Right? The plethora of choices and trying to decide on which cheescake to have, is part of the fun. Call me unadventurous, but I always get the White Chocolate Macadamia Nut! It's my favorite, and in my mind the best! But that's always a matter of personal opinion. All of the cheesecake here is exceptional! It happened to be my daughter's birthday. The waiter brought her cheescake to the table with a candle. It was beautifully presented with the words "happy birthday" written on the plate's border in chocolate syrup. Nice. So, in the end, I'd characterize this visit to TCF as fine. I'm disappointed in the reduction in portion size, though, as this has always been part of the TCF's niche. I think I left this as a tip, but always do the 30-minute call-ahead seating. Oh, BTW, they did remove my daughter's entree (the one with the hair), from the bill.

text: Finally! I'd been wanting to try Izzo's for ages, but had never had the opportunity. I had heard it was in the same vein as my beloved Felipe's, and since I heard that there will soon be an Izzo's on the Westbank, I was eager to give it a shot and see what was in store for me when one opened around the corner. So, by now you know that Izzo's has a "cafeteria" style way of serving. You go up, and you can pick what kind of tortilla you want: spicy, wheat, white, or spinach, and wait a few minutes while your burrito is rolled. The spinach tortilla intrigued me, but since it was my first time, I went with the basic white flour tortilla. I got it stuffed with pork carnitas, rice, black beans, lettuce, tomato, jalapeños, cheese, guac and green sauce. Does that sound like a lot? Yeah, it was a ton! They put it together for me, rolled it, handed it over and served it with a drink for about 10 bucks. The burrito was really dense, well made and good. I couldn't finish it all and I was happy to have plenty of leftovers. My friend and I also split some chips and queso, which was fantastic and plenty enough for both of us (we didn't even finish it all). You don't have to get a burrito here, of course. You can also get a quesadilla, nachos or tacos, but most come for the burrito. So, my final verdict? 4 fast food stars. Is it as good as Felipe's? Nah. Felipe's gives you way more bang, flavor and selection for your buck, but I wouldn't skip this place if I were in Metairie, and I certainly won't hesitate to pay it a visit when it comes to my neck of the woods.

text: Went here on 10/19 and had a flawless meal. We (party of 2) were there to celebrate a special occasion, and we made the right choice in coming to Little Country Gentleman. The menu consists of a 3 course option ($38), a 6 course option ($68) and the "chef's tasting" which is 12-13 courses ($98). If you opt for the 3 courses, you can choose from 1 of 2 options for each course. Note: I do not eat meat and the staff was more than willing to accommodate my restrictions. We opted for the 6 course option with wine pairings. There were 3 meat courses on this tasting, but the chef was able to substitute fish for me. I could go into detail about each of the six courses, but it'd be easier to simply sum up the meal as outstanding (and give a special shout out to the slow cooked egg that rocked my world). The wine pairings were especially superb. The sommelier and chef really understand the art of great food and great wine. The chef uses molecular gastronomy wisely and sparingly to enhance dishes. For example, creating pine nut dust that somehow melts in your mouth into a velvety consistency. The whole evening was really a joy and a wonderful experience. The staff is extremely attentive (bordering on TOO attentive, perhaps), and the food is inventive, exciting and most importantly, delicious. This was the best meal I've had in St. Louis since moving here from NYC 3 years ago. I also believe that this restaurant rivals some of the best in NY. Also, a nice touch: complimentary cookies in to go bags as you leave. This place achieves classiness without being overly pretentious. FANTASTIC!

text: I've been meaning to write this review for a while but kept forgetting. My visit was back on July 8, for what it's worth, so maybe things have improved? First, let me say that I had extremely high expectations for this spa. And when I first walked in, I was already planning all the wonderful things I was going to have to say about it. I'll go ahead and start with the positives. The building is gorgeous, the people were incredibly friendly, the robes were fantastic, the showers were amazing, the bathroom supplies were great, they gave me wine between services (but I had three services and was only offered a drink after the first two -- seems like I should have been offered something after the first service as well), and they had fruit and pound cake to snack on in the relaxation/waiting room in between services. Seems like this review should be a 5-star review, or at least a 4, right? Well, then there were the services. First, I started with a massage. The massage was firmly a 2-star massage on Yelp's scale. It wasn't bad, it just wasn't great. The therapist didn't really listen to my requests, so the massage was a bit of a disappointment. Next up, facial. Now the facial was pretty great. Definitely a 4-star-worthy experience. And actually, the massage time during the facial was MUCH better than the actual massage service had been. My facialist person did a great job, although I was kind of surprised that there wasn't an extraction phase. Really, the only thing keeping the facial from 5-stars was the fact that the facialist was supposed to leave me some samples up front, but they were out of the products she recommended for me, so no samples for me. At the prices of these services, I definitely wanted my samples. How else am I supposed to decide if I want to purchase the recommended products? Finally, I ended with the agave nectar pedicure. If I could give this portion of the experience fewer than 1 star, I would. Now, the lady doing the pedicure was incredibly nice. But. When I go for a pedicure, I expect my feet to leave in great shape and I expect my toes not to look like they were polished by a small child. I have never had a pedicure that looked this awful. I immediately went home and removed the polish and just did my toenails myself. There was polish all over my toes, not just on my nails. Nails weren't fully covered. Nails weren't smooth. Again, the worst pedicure I have ever had. I don't understand how a place could employ someone this bad. So in sum, a great facility, and I might could recommend this place if you're going only for a facial. But my pedicure experience really ruined the whole experience for me. It is really not acceptable to need to go re-paint your toes IMMEDIATELY after getting them "done." Waste of money. :(

We were fortunate enough to be the first guests of the evening so we had the whole place and the servers all to ourselves. We snacked on chips and salsa while looking over a very simple and defined menu. Our server said that everything on the menu was made from scratch. I though to myself, "Yeah right, they all say that," but I gave her the benefit of the doubt. I decided on the "Stacked;" a shredded beef (or chicken, or pork) dish baked between two corn tortillas, smothered in (I chose both) green chile and red chile sauce, and topped with a fried egg and melted cheese. DISCLAIMER: I am 100% Mexican and my mother makes a very similar dish that is fantastic. This dish was absolutely AMAZING!! The red sauce was as authentic as it gets; you could taste the freshness. I had no intention of eating everything, but I couldn't resist. It was THAT good! My wife had the fish tacos and those were delicious. My father-in-law had the Yucatan Enchiladas with shrimp and fish. That was great too! Even my kids' nachos were fantastic and very unique. This is my new favorite Mexican restaurant. Too bad it's so far away. Kudos to Cafe del Rio, Virginia City!

text: This is one of my favorite running trails in STL. If you go from end to end, its about 16 miles. I love this trail because it is flat (for those of you who are serious runners, it does slightly incline going from Crestwood/South County up to Kirkwood, so I would recommend starting south so that when you come back, you hit the downhill path!) and it doesn't get too busy. I've run this trail after work in the early evenings and it isn't too packed, and on weekends it generally starts getting busier around 9 a.m. There are lots of different people who use this trail from runners, walkers, bikers (who all usually announce as they are passing and don't try to mow you over like they do at other parks!) so it's always a nice mixture of people. The trail itself is nicely paved and you pass by Grant's Farm and the Clydesdales which is fun. If you are looking for mostly flat, down and back trail, this is the one to try!

I knew that my boyfriend would like to join us, as he is a fan of the Greek Food Festival each year, he agreed and even offered to treat us for the meal. We met in the lobby and placed our order promptly, at about 7:45. Mom wanted the chicken pita wrap with extra tsziki sauce; I ordered the chicken pilaf bowl; and my fellow ordered the Friday night chicken dinner special (lemon chicken with potatoes and Greek salad) which was the hostess' suggestion; we were delighted to see that the stuffed grape leaves were also a Friday special, so of course we had to order them! $52 was the total tab, but we figured that we were getting a lot of food. We were told at around 8:15 that the food was almost ready to box up, so I suggested that my guy should go home and feed his cat before joining mom and I at my house. The food was not ready until almost 8:45. At some point the gal out front said that they had run short on the chicken and had to prepare more for our order. By the time I got home with the order (I live across town by the airport) it was about 9:20 and we were all famished. I heard my boyfriend groaning when he opened his cardboard container...looking over his shoulder, I saw 2 chicken LEGS and about a cup and a half of chopped potato pieces - THIS was his $16 chicken dinner special?? For what they charge, they should tell you straight up what pieces you get in this meal. My guy liked the taste of the chicken, but honestly, it was not enough food for him for dinner and he is not a big man. I opened my chicken pilaf bowl and couldn't find the feta cheese or the tsziki sauce that is supposed to come with it, nor could I find the extra tsziki sauce that cost $1.50 (my mom wanted that). The chicken wasn't so bad, but the rice was dreadful: sticky, over-cooked and over-powering in lemon flavor (almost too tart). This rice was also included with the grape leaves, which closely resembled meatballs (not the tender, rice and meat stuffed dolmades I've had elsewhere, like in Greece) They were not seasoned, greasy, and actually left imprints on the rice "bed" beneath, I would assume because they were so heavy. The only person who was satisfied was my mom, who said her pita was delicious. Of course, her feta and tsziki sauce weren't MIA, so I'm sure hers wasn't so bad. I will also make note that the grilled pita wedges we received were very good...but would have been better if we could have dipped them in some tszki sauce (the extra that we paid for and did not receive) I called the restaurant and spoke with the manager, who said he was sorry that the chicken dinner didn't meet our expectations and would pass it along to the owner. He also apologized about the missing items, but I had to ask if he would provide them if we came back over there (which we didn't, because our intention was to dine together at home and watch a movie). I don't like to speak poorly about any establishment, but after this experience, I truly felt like a victim of P.T. Barnum: a true sucker, and no, I will not give this place another chance.

text: TL;DR - Excellent location, great price, lovely courtyards, lackluster service, disappointing room. My family and I decided on this hotel above all the others in its price range almost solely because of the photos of adorably-decorated rooms full of charming antique reproductions and beautfiul secluded courtyards. When we arrived, we were greeted by less-than-enthusiastic staff. Different staff members we encountered on subsequent days were much more friendly. We were led through a winding maze of old buildings, which lent a "secret garden" feel to the whole affair that I absolutely loved. The layout really is very fun. The courtyards really are as adorable as pictured. They're shaded and breezy - a great place to sit and enjoy your morning coffee. As we walked past some of the rooms facing the courtyards, we noticed several broken shutters, which didn't give a very good impression. The rooms... not what I expected. We had selected standard rooms. Of course I didn't expect them to be as charming as the "deluxe" rooms (which are what you see in many of the room photos for this hotel), but I did expect them to be in good repair. We were given two adjoining rooms, and both rooms had charming French doors and great climate control, but the fun stops there. The room was a decent size, and it was clean enough, but it had way too much furniture. A pair of chairs, a large table and a floor lamp completely blocked the walkway to the adjoining room, so we ended up having to move our furniture in order to make it functional. When I attempted to sit on one of these chairs, I found that it was broken and would've probably fallen through if I'd put my full weight on it. The bed in my room was very uncomfortable - very saggy in the center. Walking around, it seemed like every floor surface (carpet and tile) was covered in a slippery Pledge-like sheen (Scotchgard maybe?) - if you're not careful, you can easily wipe out and land on your face. In the bathroom, the tub surround was cracked, our shower curtain was torn and hanging off several hooks, and our mirror was chipped around the edges. Furthermore, our room had no windows - we had two sets of French Doors, but one set had no shutters on its windows so it needed to be covered by heavy drapes. As a result, the room felt dark and gloomy. The adjoining room was better. They had a comfortable bed, a more spacious layout, chairs that weren't broken, and two large windows that made their room feel bright and cheerful. The first night we were there, I dipped my feet into the beautiful large pool near the main courtyard. I was impressed with it - it was an even nicer space than the photos suggested. The smaller pool was interesting, in a tiny courtyard, surrounded on two sides by low-hanging plants, but equally pretty and inviting. The following morning, however, I got a better look at those pools in the daylight and found them to be ABSOLUTELY FILTHY. What I thought was a dark-colored bottom was actually a light-blue bottom nearly completely covered in dark algae and dirt. They obviously take the time to skim off the debris - even the small pool that has trees hanging into it was clear of floating junk - and the filters were running, but they most certainly did not clean. They were disgusting - I can't stress this enough. I really regretted even dipping my feet into the water. It's an old building so I'm not deducting any points for this, but the rooms are not terribly quiet. Luckily, this place is in a great location (away from the chaos of Bourbon) but you will still hear people in the rooms above and near you, and there was definitely a lot of noise from the nearby staircase. It wasn't bothersome enough to disrupt sleep. Room service is apparently hit-or-miss. Our beds were always neatly made and towels and toiletries replaced, but the adjoining room didn't fare so well - they did not receive replacement washcloths or soap, so we had to share. Neither of the rooms received extra toiletpaper when that got dangerously low - we had to ask for more. The continental breakfast was actually pretty good - better than what you see at many hotels, at least - and the area of the lobby where it's served is quite nice. And it was great to have good coffee and hot tea available there 24/7. Overall, I can't say I'd choose to stay here again. The location is terrific, and the price is right, but there are so many other similar options in the area I can't help but assume that some of them must be at least a little better.

text: I recently purchased a blighted property with my siblings in Mid-City. We are historically renovating the property. We began plumbing the building and planned on replacing the existing water meter, which has not been updated since the house was originally built in 1910, with two new meters and new pipes that funnel to our water meters. I spoke to the House Connections department in SWBNO and she quoted the installation cost between $1,800 and $2,500. She explained that sometimes an installation can cost upwards of $5,000 for a meter installation, but we would only have to pay $2,500 at the most. I received the estimate ten days later: $5,068.20. This was only for one meter and we would have to pay the whole amount. When I tried to understand why it was so drastically different from the other prices I was given, they explained that it is never the SWBNO's policy to give clients average price estimates, even though two of her employees already had, and she referred me to master of maintenance. The master of maintenance had very little insight as to how the water meter installation prices were actually determined. He said this was the SWBNO's primary contractor's domain: Fleming Construction. He said Fleming Construction set the prices and SWBNO followed suit. He tried to help to the best of his ability, but the reality was that he merely managed SWBNO's contract with Fleming. I called Jefferson Parish's water board to see how much they charged for installing a one-inch water meter. They charge a flat rate of $1,500. The city pays for the pipes on public property and the homeowner pays for the portion within their property line. I discovered that most municipalities across America operate in the same fashion (Chicago, Illinois, Tucson, Arizona), and some counties go as far as incur all of the costs for new meter installation, because they regard it as standard updating and maintenance of infrastructure. Other city's water utilities provide thorough pricing schedules for different types of water meter installation scenarios. The pricing reasoning is well documented and fully accessible to the customer. This creates a predictable and fair planning environment. SWBNO's policy of expecting homeowners to foot the entire bill for maintenance and updates that should have already occurred stands in direct opposition to Mayor Landrieu and the City Council's goal of fighting blight, fixing the condition of our deteriorating streets, and minimizing city operating costs. Investors require a predictable and transparent city government. Most investors can absorb a certain amount of variable costs, but I doubt that after someone has purchased a home, and then secured a construction loan like we have, that they will be liquid enough to pay a little over $10,000 to partially subsidize a municipal service that should have been maintained. As a historic district, most of the Mid-City housing stock boasts water meters from when the neighborhood was initially drained in the 1910's. We later discovered that our existing meter was made of toxic lead. If we ever hope to address the chronic blight that has pre-dated 2005, then we must not penalize would-be investors by forcing them to pay for the mistakes of a mismanaged bureaucracy. We must fairly and efficiently address our infrastructure while also mending the structural issues of the SWBNO that have culminated in this citywide crisis. I am not an engineer, economist, or a city planner, but since no one in the SWBNO seems to hold these credentials either, I feel equally qualified in stating that updating the pipes in such a piece-meal fashion will ultimately waste time and money for the city and Orleans Parish taxpayers. In my subsequent dealings with the SWBNO I learned that it contracts out all of their engineering, maintenance, and pavement repairs to private contractors. The employees manning their offices have no immediate access to these contracts, making it impossible for home and business owners to coordinate reasonable time schedules for repairs and updates occurring on or near their properties. As the city considers another price increase for the SWBNO's services I believe we must seriously consider what services they actually provide. Much scrutiny has been directed towards the SWBNO's Director Marcia St. Martin's salary, pension plan, and performance as a director. They are well-deserved critiques and must not be abandoned. Further inspection should also be directed toward the employees of the SWBNO. There are undoubtedly many hardworking and experienced individuals at the SWBNO, but I believe those who are none of those things outnumber them by a great majority. The Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans is not just another utility company. It is charged with working against extraordinary subsidence, functioning as a stopgap against disease spurred on by standing water, and keeping our city from drowning when it rains. We have to expect better.

Lumber Liquidators is having a sale that is very appealing, and they are providing a great deal on financing. The process begins, and, as I'm a novice with a sort of odd floor plan, I have them come out and measure my house prior to my purchase to ensure that I get the right amount. The young man arrives at the appointed time, measures, gives me details about all I need, and I show up at the store and buy what he told me to. I'm spending something like $8,000 for the product alone, on sale. I finance a huge chunk of the purchase and pay cash for the rest. As home, do it yourself remodels go, this project took a long time, and I only recently finished the floor. Now here is where it get's frustrating. I've got over $800 worth of extra, un-opened, factory quality, wood left over. This is beautiful stuff, I have no qualms with the quality of the product. Now, I know it's been two years, but I'm thinking that there is something the store can do for me. I was wrong. No help. They told me to post it on Craig's list and a builder might want to take it off my hands. Yea, that's a great plan. I tell the Assistant Manager on the phone to please brainstorm all possible options and give me a call the next day. That never happens either. So, I buy $8,000 worth of floor, I pay $100 to have somebody they recommend do the measuring, I buy what I was told to buy, I store it properly for two years, I install it well, and they will not take back or credit me for the extra unopened boxes of wood. You might be wondering, 'what does the purchase order allow?' This is a great question. I re-read the agreement, and, sure enough, that's what is written in the fine print. There is a brief period of time, 90 days or so, in which to return unopened and new products. This is the part that I need to own. What was I expecting? I guess I was expecting compassion, a buyback program, some sense that they understood what I was going through. In short, something more than I got. Is the product good? Yes, heck I think it's great. My only hope at this point is that you get to benefit from my frustration. Read the contract, install in a timely fashion, and don't expect a lot of compassion from the retail outfit. I might buy their product again, but it's hard to imagine right now.

text: I arrived in MSY at 2AM on a Thursday morning. Pluses: - Easy to find. Signs are visible as soon as you come out to baggage claim. - Friendly staff. Despite it being 2AM, the lady at the counter was super nice. - The driver was very nice and helpful - only 20 dlls one way. Minuses: - We sat in the shuttle at the airport for about 35 minutes, waiting for other passengers, before taking off. What you need to know: - They will assume you're purchasing a round-trip shuttle and will ask you when you depart. If you want a one-way ride, just let them know. The lady was very nice about it and said to call them if i ended up needed to book them for a ride back. - It is a ride-share, so expect to be driven around before being dropped off at your location. This will add to your drop-off time and it is an inevitable aspect of this type of service. - There was A LONG line of people waiting for a taxi at 2AM -- the 30-minute wait in the shuttle was actually shorter than the people who stood in line waiting for a taxi. - I didn't book a shuttle ride back from my hotel to MSY since my flight was departing MSY on a Friday afternoon. You can take a taxi to the corner of TULANE & LOYOLA -- the N.O. Public Library -- and from there catch the E2 bus to the airport (takes about 45 minutes to get there) and charges you 2 dlls. Monday - Friday, this should be okay since the bus runs regularly during the day. My cab from the French Quarter to Tulane & Loyola public library cost 7 dlls. Have exact change if you take the E2 bus (there's a walgreens across the street from the library, if you need to make change).

text: I love Frankie Tocco's and eat there frequently. I've tried a number of their pasta dishes and absolutely loved the baked cannelloni and Rigatoni di Tocco. Both are rich and savory and consistently top of the line. Portions are large so if you have an appetizer or salad, be prepared to take home part of your entree. Their garlic cheese bread is phenomenal and the cannelloni bites appetizer are fried bits of goodness served with their amazing Italian gravy and a sprinkle of fresh shredded parmesano-reggiano. My husband loves their fried mushrooms, an easy app to fail on due to the need to cook them long enough so the insides are done but not so much that they are like chewing acorns. Salads are great, a mix of iceberg and spring greens and the Tocco special salad is a meal unto itself. House dressing is a balance of not too sharp and not too sweet Italian. The restaurant is definitely a smaller family affair but that appeals to me. I like feeling like I'm in my neighbor's home with family photos on the walls. Sure, the booths may have a spot or two of wear but to me that adds to the charm. I've seen reports of slow service in other reviews but never experienced that myself. I've had consistently good service, frequent check-ins by staff and even by Mama Tocco herself, who can usually be found in the family booth. This is definitely a favorite place for our family and an area gem!

text: Lolita is a nuevo mexican cantina located on 13th and Sansom right next door to Barbuzzo. This is an important piece of information, for otherwise you could walk up and down 13th and not locate this place. It is a small joint (seats less than 70) and has it's name written in light grey on the bottom panel of the glass wall. Even after you discover it, you would wonder if this is not an extension to Barbuzzo itself, and indeed on the sidewalk it's hard to tell where the outside seating of one restaurant ends and where the other's begins. Seems fortunate, or maybe it is by design, that the owners are the same for the two places. Whether there is some deep aesthetic reason behind this occult appearance, or it's merely a gimmick, Lolita succeeds in drawing throngs of customers. It doesn't take reservations by phone or the web, it doesn't accept credit cards although entrees are priced higher than $20, the servers are efficient but brusque; in other words, it does its part in trying to drive away the hordes, but it is oh-so-crowded. Especially on weekend nights. My friend asked how does the phenomenon occur, and frankly I was not 100% satisfied with the answer the Lolita experience provided. Lolita is a B.Y.O.T(equila) place, and so in the half an hour we were asked to wait before we could get our table, we popped into a liquor store and bought a bottle of 100% agave 'juice'. While checking out, the cashier took one look at us four people buying a single bottle and remarked, "Must be for Lolita!", stressing and lingering on the last syllable long enough to lend it a mischievous lilt. (For me, personally, that was the harbinger of the night ahead - but that's another story.) We eventually got into the restaurant, hungry and thirsty, and immediately ordered off a pitcher of the traditional lime margarita. Another quirky thing about this place is that all the food must be ordered at the same time. For a moment, I feared all the food will appear at the same time as well. Fortunately that was not the case. We ordered two vegetarian appetizers. The traditional guacamole was garnished with jicamas and served alongside three kinds of chips, the usual corn, plantain and colcassia (or arvi as we call it in India), and salsa both verde and traditional. The beet and mango salad was served with arugula and a plantain pakoda, dolloped with soft goat cheese. The guac was a little too salty, and the salad had nothing outstanding about it either. The margarita, on the other hand, was pretty fabulous. For entree, I went with the carne asada - medium-rare tenderloin served in a mash of creamy plantain on top of fried yuccas along side traditional salsa. The meat was succulent, and the dull taste of the plantain crema went well with it. The semi-crunchy yuccas also interspersed well with the sinewy meat. I tasted a bit from the other's as well: the salmon and the veggie enchilada seemed a bit mediocre compared to the beef, although the fried tofu in the latter was a treat. Summary: Lolita is a bit on the expensive side, and frankly I do not see why I would choose this place over El Vez which is right opposite it. The latter takes reservations, accepts credit cards, is much more expansive and has a better decor. Nonetheless, the food and margarita is decent, and I would recommend Lolita if you have been to El Vez before - at least twice.

text: So if you spin a tale about how you allegedly studied the fine art of bread making with some famous dude in Italy, does it make your pizza customers give you way more stars than your food/service actually deserve? Apparently. Every time I go in this place I expect Ashton Kutcher to jump from under my booth and scream "punked again!" From the "I know you ordered a veggie lovers pizza but my stoned assistant made you a meat lovers so eat it & smile, bitch" to the selling you a fountain soda and giving you a totally blank look when you ask for your money back because of the "broke" sign on said soda machine that they were clearly aware of when they sold you the soda. I sometimes wonder if Natty doesn't videotape the clustetfuck interactions with his customers just to have something to watch and laugh at when the shop closes. This place is consistently inconsistent folks. And proscuitto garlic knots does not a good pizza shop make. Sure the garlic knots are good but I've come here for PIZZA - not some lame excuse for using up the dough. Sure Natty is nice to share his life story with you but again - doesn't translate to delicious pizza in my pie hole by the end of said life story telling. THIS PIZZA SUCKS. I actually happen to be in the 1% of native St. Louis people who actually know what a New York style pizza is supposed to be. How is that, you ask? Because I worked at the long gone but not forgotten fabulous pizza place called Brooklyn Bridge Pizzeria during the 80s. The place where the owner, Steve, would crack your knuckles with the hot pizza paddle if the pizza u made wasn't perfect in every way. If that guy hadn't taken his pride & ego back to New York when he hit a snag with the health department Brooklyn Bridge Pizza would still be serving hundreds of slices & pies per day & the likes of Natty's & Racanellis would be laughed out of business with their lame attempts at New York pizza. New York pizza is supposed to have a crisp crust with a slight crunch to go with the chew. The crust should be able to hold the pizza up when you lift it to bite - not be a runny, drippy sloppy mess as is the case at Natty's. Most times the crust at Natty's is still doughy which tells me his oven temp & cooking time for the pizza is WAY off. Every time I have eaten here I have overheard at least one phone call from a delivery & one conversation in the restaurant about how they are dissatisfied with their pizza here. How does he stay in business? Because so many are willing to trade liking the pizza here for liking the quirky, eccentric owner here. I like him, too. The obvious embellishments in his life story tale make him interesting & endearing. They do not, however, make him a man who understands the fine art of New York style pizza making. BYOB - you betcha - you're going to need it to help you drown your disappointment when you realize this is just another crap pizza joint in a City already overcrowded with crap pizza joints.

text: I'm updating my review since I had the unfortunate bad luck of ending up in the hospital last week. I had been having flu like symptoms and was diagnosed with stomach flu at the doctor. Yep, NINE HOURS. It took that long to get in, get triaged, get a CT scan, and get seen by a doctor. Then get seen by the doctor again. Then wait for transport to my room. It was so ridiculous that the nurse told me, after I finally got put into a room, that I was next to be seen. It took forever. And then some. I'm sure there were sicker people there. But my doctor was outside my room almost the whole time. He wasn't rushing to see emergencies. I FINALLY got taken to my room. I had requested a private room because I was having some pretty nasty GI symptoms and needed my own bathroom and privacy. And of course, they rolled me up to a double - occupied- room. I lost it. It was 1:30am, I was feeling like shit, and I threw a toddler quality tantrum. No one cared. They pretty much forced me in the room. I had no choice. I was on the "waiting list" for a private room. I never got it, after FOUR DAYS of being in the hospital, every doctor treating me requesting it for me, asking every nurse I had, my dad calling the admitting department, talking to the floor coordinator more than once, and basically begging. But... the care does not make up for my excruciating time in the ER and my humiliation in not being able to get a private room. I don't think I can ever come back here. text: Renting apartments is a huge headache, right? This past summer I found out that it doesn't really have to be. I had a great experience renting through Philip Barron and definitely recommend them for anyone looking for a great apartment in the Clayton area... there were a few bumps along the way but overall they've been great to work with and I absolutely love my apartment... so much that I plan on renewing again when my lease is up in August. The renting process itself was pretty darn easy, and I love that they only charged a month's rent for the security deposit (I've experienced way worse than that.) The whole process took less than two weeks, and I got to move into my gorgeous little place. Pretty seamless, right? The only issue was with cleaning. Before I moved in, I went to look around and saw that the place was pretty dirty (think long dark hair everywhere, grease on the stove and backup in the dishwasher... so gross.) The cleaning crew assured me that they'd have it looking great soon, but when I moved in it was still so dirty and the dishwasher was the exact same way. Major sadface. They sent someone back to clean it some more but I ended up hiring my own cleaning crew because at that point I didn't trust PB to do it themselves. $200 to have your place cleaned after you just moved in definitely stings a little bit! Overall, though, they've been great. I recently had an AC issue and someone from maintenance came right over and fixed it, and they're pretty attentive and willing to help with whatever I need. Now if only they could do something about my downstairs neighbors...

text: We were at Tzin for my birthday last friday and it was to die for! I really had no idea how small the place was. I read it was small, but had no idea it was THAT small. It's super cute, cozy, and comfortable, considering it's size. I loved every inch of the place, though, and hope to go back again. We got there a touch early, and our table for six hadn't come up yet, so we were seated at the bar, poured complimentary champagne and wine until some seats opened up for us and Kelsey (the owner or manager?) treated us like we were close friends of her's. One resounding comment amongst our group was that the music was a bit too loud. Subsequently, everyone in the room has to be loud, so the server couldn't hear our order, and we had to ask him to repeat himself when listing off the desserts. That said - food - AMAZING (crab stuffed prawns, baked brie with pear/cran compote, and flourless choc. cake - YUM - YUM - YUM); the wine selection was impeccable, and the atmosphere is exactly what we expected. A cool, chic, friendly little place I hope to visit again, and again, and again. Tip to Yelpers - RESERVATIONS ARE A MUST. We originally planned a party of ten, and I'm glad a couple people cancelled - we would have overwhelmed the place! Go with an open mind (for those of you who think/call yourselves claustraphobic) and an empty stomach, and you won't be sorry. Cheers!

Just toast it when you defrost ;) Their Cuban sandwiches also rank among my favorites...actually they might be my favorite. ;) When I lived in Tampa I would stop by here every opportunity I had. My only complaint is that their early hours (5pm on weekdays, 3pm on Saturday, and 1pm on Sunday) make it very difficult for someone with a 9-5 job to catch them when they are open. The bakery is family run and well worth supporting.

text: I've had an abysmal experience with Member Solutions. In trying to cancel a contract, I have had to provide countless proofs of relocation. Yet Member Solutions will not cancel the contract. I understand the benefits of using Member Solutions for small businesses. Holding customers to their contracts is important. Yet small businesses interested in these types of services should reconsider using Member Solutions. They will drive your customers crazy. Here are some reasons why: 1. They are inconsistent: Member Solutions said, a month ago, that 1 form of proof I submitted for relocation was sufficient, then, this month, said it was insufficient. In other words, they changed their policy on the fly and provided no justification for doing so. This drives people crazy. Instead of solving your membership issues, this inconsistency will cause your customers to come back to you angry about their membership issues. 2. They are ineffectual: The customer service representatives at Member Solutions use phrases like "I understand your frustration," and, "I can see how that would be tough," but do not actually help. In a recent conversation, a representative told me that, while he "understands my frustration," he cannot make a decision regarding my case. The power to make this decision lies with someone else. "Can I talk to the people with the power to make decisions?" I asked. "No, they do not accept calls" he said. So, in dealing with the customer service representatives, nothing actually gets done except clumsy therapy. This drives people crazy. Your customers will come back to you to get something done. Thus, defeating the purpose of employing Member Solutions. 3. They are anonymous and negative: People like small businesses because they get to see people face to face, and get to use first names. People like gyms because they are positive environments that make them feel better. By outsourcing your membership issues to Member Solutions, what you had going for you, as a small business and a gym, quickly disintegrates. Member Solutions is anonymous. The representatives are reluctant to tell you who they are and who is in charge. They build zero trust. As well, dealing with Member Solutions is negative. They make honest and paying customers, like me, feel like irresponsible and helpless idiots for signing a contract. By being treated like an anonymous "anybody," and by being made to feel like an irresponsible and helpless idiot for signing a contract, Member Solutions will cause your customers to grow resentful of your small business and gym. What you'll gain in short term convenience, you'll lose in long term trust. I realize the pressures on small businesses. If there were a membership service that was consistent, effectual, transparent, and positive--I would have no problems with it. Indeed, if a membership service was doing a good job, they probably wouldn't call much attention to themselves. As you can see by the very fact that I, a customer, am wasting my weekend to write about this company, you should be suspicious of their services. They call attention to themselves. And, because their procedures are inconsistent (etc.), I perceive the small businesses they represent in a similar light. I really enjoyed my experiences at the gym using Member Solutions, but, because of my experience with Member Solutions, I will not go back to the gym, ever, or advise others to go back there. It's that bad. In sum, I have had a horrible experience with this company, and plan to let others know about my experiences (far and wide). For the good of your small business, I would recommend shopping around for another membership service--or---perhaps--dealing with these inevitable (frustrating, but trust-building) issues on your own.
label: NEG
